title: Process: branch-from-main + real-report merge gate
description:
## Background
User rule: for each feature/gap, cut a branch from main; after implement, run REAL scenarios; merge to main ONLY when report matches expectation.

## Technical approach (every feature bead must follow)
1. git checkout main && git pull
2. git checkout -b feat/<id>-short-slug (or fix/)
3. Implement + unit tests in lk-sim (and target .agent-sim only if needed)
4. build/typecheck/test green
5. Real execute: lk-sim execute <scenario> --root <voice-ai-worker or target>
6. Inspect reports/<run-id>/summary.json + events + web if needed
7. Merge only if status/assert/script pass as expected (or documented draft waiver)

## Success criteria
- Written checklist used on each feature
- No direct commits to main for multi-file features
- Report path cited in bead close reason

## Considerations
- DTMF scenarios may be draft until worker handles digits — close with draft note, not fake green
- If LiveKit/Gemini flaky: pass@k, then re-research before blaming code
close_reason: Adopted as standing process: every feature branches from main; merge only with real scenario report (or explicit DTMF draft waiver). Documented in bead + WIP.

title: P1+: DTMF real E2E when a target agent consumes SIP DTMF
description:
## Background

## Success
Real execute report where agent reacts to sim.dtmf; then lift draft waiver.
close_reason: Real DTMF E2E achieved (PR #94). Fixed the dtmf runtime path (if-wait→elif-wait): dtmf steps now publish the tone + emit sim.script.dtmf instead of being clobbered to sim.script.cue and masking with '[DTMF: N]' speech. Live run 058-press-4 verified: sim.script.dtmf {digits:'4'} recorded, agent reacted ('You pressed 4. Transferring you to a human agent now.'). Full pytest 669 passed. Agent worker intermittently down afterward (external infra), but the E2E proof exists.

comments.author: ADMIN
comments.text: Reflect 2026-07-30: Still OPEN. No real E2E DTMF test against a live agent. src/ has DTMF script action code (DRAFT) but no real report verification.

comments.author: ADMIN
comments.text: Real DTMF E2E achieved (PR #94). Investigation revealed a code bug: dtmf steps fell into the speak/else branch of ScriptRunner._fire() (else bound to 'if wait'), clobbering kind to sim.script.cue and injecting '[DTMF: N]' as speech — so the agent reacted to spoken words, not a tone, and no sim.script.dtmf event was recorded. Fixed with if-wait→elif-wait (chain: if-dtmf/elif-wait/elif-hang_up/else-speak); dtmf now publishes the tone + emits sim.script.dtmf (Rust-port parity). Verified live run 058-press-4: events.jsonl contains sim.script.dtmf {action:dtmf, digits:'4'}, no cue/mask; agent replied 'You pressed 4. Transferring you to a human agent now.' Full pytest 669 passed. Note: the dtmf-demo-local agent worker went intermittently unavailable afterward (dispatch.agent_timeout) — external infra, not a code regression.

title: Process: one-gap-one-PR merge gate (tests+build+real report; portable core)
description:
## Standing process (user 2026-07-14)

**One gap / one feature = one PR into main.** No bundling, no silent merge of multiple beads.

### Merge-ready PR requires ALL of:
1. **Unit tests** green for the change (`uv run pytest` relevant + full suite before merge)
2. **Build** green (`uv sync` / package importable; web build if web touched)
3. **Real execute** against a **running** LiveKit agent (any black-box target via `--root <target>/.agent-sim`) with a **real report** under `reports/<run-id>/` where status/assert/script gate matches expectation
4. **Portable core** — AGENTS.md: never hardcode worker/dashboard/product keys in `src/`. Target is only a smoke root; core must work for any LiveKit agent.

### Explicitly forbidden
- Fitting core logic to voice-ai-worker or any one monorepo
- Merging without real report when the surface is runtime (script/assert/telephony/persona)
- Fake-green reports (e.g. DTMF when agent never consumes digits)
- Multiple features in one PR

### Draft PRs
Allowed when E2E cannot be honest yet (e.g. DTMF until some target handles SIP DTMF). Draft must say what is missing; not merge until real report exists.

### Branch naming
`feat/<bead-or-id>-short-slug` from latest main.
close_reason: Documented in WIP.md PR/merge process; enforced going forward: one gap one PR; tests+build+real report; portable core.

description: Rewrite the Python package livekit-agent-simulator (lks, ~25.1 kLOC / 105 files) in Rust as a fine-grained crates workspace rooted at src/livekit_agent_simulator_rust/. Goal: a single static binary with identical on-disk artifacts (events.jsonl, runs.sqlite, summary.json, meta.json, conversation.wav), identical config/scenario compatibility, and the same 21 MCP tools + 23 CLI commands. Source of truth: docs/plans/PLAN-20260813-rust-full-port.md (Rev 3a) + docs/plans/rust-port-appendices/{A-web-layer-spec,C-wire-protocols,D-phases-edge-cases,review-verify-20260813}.md. Invariants I1-I10 in the plan are the contract: report format byte-compatible, sqlite DDL byte-identical, config/scenario compatible, caller brain parity, SimLeg topology parity. Phases P0-P10 + P3.5. Python remains the reference until P10; any divergence is a port bug. Workspace is FINE-GRAINED crates (D1, decided 2026-08-13): lks-core / lks-livekit / lks-web / lks-mcp / lks-plugins / lks (binary) + vendored gemini-live + agent-sim-proto. Key reason for the split: P0/P1 (config/scenario) must build and test WITHOUT building libwebrtc (livekit crate pulls C++ libwebrtc) — lks-core stays libwebrtc-free until P2. [2026-08-13 03:59:20 UTC] CROSS-CUTTING INVARIANTS (apply to every phase):
1. Python parity is the contract. Python remains the reference implementation until P10; any divergence is a port bug (recorded as an issue with a pinned Python-side golden). Observer: lk.transcription text streams (TextStreamOpened topic=='lk.transcription', read lk.transcription_final/lk.segment_id attributes attrs.get(...).lower()=='true'; read_all FULL stream plain text not JSON; empty text dropped; role agent iff participant_identity==agent_identity else user). lk.agent.session byte streams -> prost-decoded AgentSessionMessage (framing: accumulate ALL chunks, parse ONE concatenated proto per byte stream NOT length-prefixed; observer.error on parse failure). 9. Audio: ParallelMicMixer (room_pcm cues + caller voice mixing with gain, saturating sum int(round(s*gain)) clamped [-32768,32767], effects post-mix to exact bytes agent hears, capture_frame ALWAYS even for silence, speech preroll 150ms no zero-punch, end_speech_turn drains with silence pad). LocalConversationRecorder (conversation.wav 16kHz PCM16 stereo L=sim/R=agent; mark_start() pins recorder t=0 right after track publish; gap-pad only when gap_s>0.02). 10. caller_nudge.rs full contract: AGENT_GREETED_NUDGE='(The agent has finished greeting you. Respond now in the language of your persona.)' NON-AUDIBLE activation. Gate: first_speaker!='agent' -> return no event; silent -> sim.agent_greeted_nudge_skipped {reason:'silent_mode'}. Loop poll 0.15s: agent_has_spoken and not user_has_spoken -> sleep 1.0s debounce -> re-check end_call/user_has_spoken (abort silently) -> bridge.nudge_freestyle_answer; success -> sim.agent_greeted_nudge {debounce_s:1.0,audible:False} return. RuntimeError -> sleep 0.15s retry. Orchestrator creates task ONLY when run.first_speaker=='agent' and not scenario.script_steps and not _silent; cancelled in finally. Runner: emit sim.interrupt_rate ONCE at start (spec keys exactly rate,interval_ms,class,say,asset,delivery,min_agent_active_ms; source='sim.interrupt_rate' include_dialogue=False). Loop poll 0.05s; armed bursts; recently_spoke=last_agent_activity within 3.0s; agent_active=agent_is_active_speaker or recently_spoke; skip events sim.interrupt_rate_skip {reason:'agent_not_active',active_ms}/{reason:'active_ms_below_min',active_ms,min}; _fire step_id 'rate-barge-{n}' from 1; blip when with_blip && delivery!='room_pcm' inject '[barge blip]' label '{step_id}-blip' delivery room_pcm asset 'builtin:noise.blip'; interruption event ONLY if agent_is_active_speaker at fire AND no inject error (spec {by:'sim',barge_in:True,class,false_positive:class in (noise,backchannel),step_id,label,say,note:'Interrupt-rate barge while agent was active speaker'}); sim.script.cue ALWAYS emitted per fire incl error field with full key set.

title: P3.5 — Web report player + REST API (parity)
description:
Web report player + REST API parity (crates/lks-web). Port the two HTTP servers and the full cues-report pipeline: (1) report UI server port 8765 serving the embedded SPA (web/dist via rust-embed) + /api/runs* JSON + /runs/<id>/* file routes; (2) REST API server port 8787 prefix /api/v1 bridging to the ops layer; (3) cues.json pipeline — report_time (timing base), source_priority, windows, transcript_cues (dedupe + ghost-STT), markers, tool_events, speech_origin, cues payload assembly. Byte-parity target: cues.json output identical to Python web/cues.py for the same report dir (golden-tested); header-level parity for HTTP (exact Content-Type / Cache-Control / no-store / 302 semantics). Runs after P3 (report files exist on disk) and before P4. Until then POST /api/v1/execute|validate|preflight return op-stub shapes (web only guarantees status codes + error mapping, payload shapes ops-owned).

Files: crates/lks-web/src/{mod,report_server,api_server,cues,report_time,source_priority,windows,transcript_cues,markers,tool_events,speech_origin,static_assets}.rs + assets/web/ (web/dist embed) + tests/{parity_cues,web_routes,cues_constants,markers,speech_origin,transcript_dedupe,static_serving,range_requests,api_errors}.rs. Depends on lks-core (report_dir reading, ops stubs) + lks-livekit (behavior_summary recompute).

STEPS (implement in this order; report_time first — everything depends on it):
1. report_time.rs: wav_duration_ms(path)->Option<i64> int(frames*1000/rate) hound frames rate=getframerate() or 1 any error->None. load_events skip empty lines skip JSON-fail lines per-line missing->[]. load_json missing/corrupted->{} non-object->{}. resolve_audio_t0_ms(meta,events)->i64 meta.audio.t0_mono_ms int max(0,) else first event kind starts 'transcript.' or kind in {sim.mic_published,sim.gemini_connected}->max(0,ts_mono_ms) else 0. mono_to_audio_ms(mono,t0,duration_ms)->Option<i64> start=max(0,mono-t0); if duration_ms Some and start>duration_ms+2000->None. clamp_end(start,end,duration_ms)->i64 end=max(start+120,end); if duration end=min(end,max(start+120,duration_ms)). NO datetime formatting in this module (only the run-list sort key parses dates).
2. source_priority.rs: SIM_CALLER_SOURCES=['sim.gemini','sim.openai']; USER table sim.gemini=0 sim.openai=0 data=2 lk.transcription=3; AGENT table data=0 lk.transcription=1 sim.gemini=2 sim.openai=2. source_rank(source,role): exact table match role=='user' (any other role->agent table); else source non-empty AND not in {sim.gemini,sim.openai,lk.transcription}->opaque data-topic 1(user)/0(agent); else (empty or builtin-not-in-table)->9. texts_similar(a,b): normalize lowercase+strip; remove apostrophes ' ' '; re.sub(r'[^\w\s]',' ',t); collapse whitespace; either empty->false; match iff a_n==b_n or a_n in b_n or b_n in a_n. Token-canonical _ASR_TOKEN_ALIASES={okey:okay,ok:okay,k:okay,thank:thanks,thx:thanks,byebye:bye} per whitespace token; inter=ta∩tb; true iff inter.len()>=max(1,int(min(len(ta),len(tb))*0.5+0.5)) round-half-up min 1.
3. windows.rs: estimate_utterance_ms(text,role): empty->800(agent)/600(user). words=split on ' ' after \n->' ' keeping non-empty; units=max(len(words),max(1,len(text)/4)) integer division; ms=units*(95 if agent else 85); clamp agent [700,22000] user [500,14000]. collect_interim_starts: kinds transcript.*.interim role from 'agent'/'user' in kind text=spec.text stripped skip empty ms via mono_to_audio_ms skip None. collect_agent_active_windows: from room.active_speakers events; agent_on iff any identity starts_with('agent-') or 'agent' in identity.to_lowercase(); missing/empty identities->off; non-list spec.identities->[]. points sorted by ms; gap_close_ms=2800: while on if gap since last-on>2800 close window (start,last_on+600) start new; on off close (start,last_on+600). trailing window end last_on+600 capped duration_ms. merge pass if w0<=prev_w1+1500 merge. best_interim_start(interims,role,final_ms,text,est_ms,prefer_source)->Option<i64> window_lo=max(0,final_ms-est_ms-3000) window_hi=final_ms-500 if window_hi<=window_lo->None; candidate match 12-char truncated prefix either direction; rank=source_rank(src,role); if prefer_source==Some(s) and src==s rank=-1; sort (rank,ms) return min ms among best rank. best_active_window(windows,final_ms,est_ms) keep windows where final_ms>=w0-300 && final_ms<=w1+2000; span=max(1,w1-w0); score=abs(w1-final_ms)+abs(span-est_ms)/3 integer division; lowest score wins ->(w0,w1).
4. transcript_cues.rs: pipeline raw->dedupe->ghost filter->timing->final sort. Raw cues from transcript.user.final/transcript.agent.final: fields role,final_ms,text,turn,source,kind,ts_mono_ms (final_ms from mono_to_audio_ms skip None; non-int ts_mono_ms skip). Dedupe max_delta: sort raw by (final_ms,source_rank,0 if role=='agent' else 1) agent first on ties. walk backward same-role: delta=abs(prev.final_ms-c.final_ms); similar=texts_similar; cross_source both non-empty different. max_delta=15000 user+similar+cross_source; 6000 agent+similar+cross_source; 4000 similar; 2500 not similar. If delta>max_delta BREAK (sorted order relied on). If similar replace cues[i] iff cur_rank<prev_rank OR (equal rank AND len(c.text)>len(prev.text)); replaced break. Not replaced append. Ghost-STT filter: only runs when >=1 user cue source in {sim.gemini,sim.openai}. Drop user cue c iff ALL: (a) src not in {sim.gemini,sim.openai}; (b) src=='lk.transcription' OR (src non-empty AND not in {sim.gemini,sim.openai,sim.script} AND 'transcript' in src); (c) exists provider user cue g abs(c.final_ms-g.final_ms)<=2500; (d) !any(texts_similar(c.text,g.text) for g in near). Non-user always kept; sim.script never dropped. Timing per cue: est=estimate_utterance_ms; agent->best_active_window ->(start,end_hint); prefer_source=Some('sim.gemini') for user else None; interim_start=best_interim_start; if interim_start<start (or start None) start=interim_start. fallback start=max(0,final_ms-est). if start>=final_ms start=max(0,final_ms-400). Clamp start=max(0,min(start,final_ms-200)). tail=350 end=final_ms+350; if end_hint>final_ms end=max(end,min(end_hint,final_ms+800)); if duration known end=min(end,max(start+200,duration_ms)); finally end=max(start+200,end). Final sort (start_ms,0 if agent else 1).
5. markers.rs kind strings verbatim: barge_in,script_cue,user_audio_source,audio_onset,silence_wait,silence,interruption,recovery,backchannel,false_interrupt,dtmf,tool,tool_error. _collect_script_injects kind sim.script_inject start=mono_to_audio_ms(ts_mono_ms) dur=int(spec.duration_ms or 0); if dur<=0 dur=2200 if delivery!='room_pcm' else 800; end_ms=start+max(200,dur); fields start_ms,duration_ms,end_ms,label,text,delivery,asset. _inject_duration_near(at_ms) candidates abs(inj.start_ms-at_ms)<=900 same if label substring or _text_overlap(label,say) score=d-(200 if same else 0) best lowest->duration_ms. sim.script.cue mtype=barge_in if spec.barge_in else script_cue; overridden by icls: backchannel->backchannel noise->false_interrupt dtmf->dtmf (icls=spec.class or spec.interrupt_class). detail='trigger={trigger or ?} · during_agent={bool}' + (' · class={icls}') + (' · say="{say}"') + (' · waited={waited}ms'). Span: if barge and icls not in (noise,backchannel): span=max(2200 if during else 1400,(inj_dur or 0)+400); else span=max(400,min(waited,2000) or 400,(inj_dur or 0)+200). end=clamp_end(start,start+span,duration_ms). Label prefix '⚡ '(barge+during not noise/backchannel) '💬 '(backchannel) '🔇 '(noise). Fields type,start_ms,end_ms,label,detail,step_id(None if empty),say(None if empty),during_agent_speech,barge_in,class,audio_ms=inj_dur or span. barge_points.append(start) only if barge && icls not in (noise,backchannel,dtmf,silence). sim.script.wait span=waited if waited>0 else 1500; win_start=max(0,start-span); end=clamp_end(win_start,start+200); type silence_wait; label=label or step_id or 'user pause'; detail 'script wait · trigger={trigger or silence} · held≈{span}ms'; fields step_id,trigger. silence.detected span=duration_ms if >0 else 4000; win_start=max(0,start-span); end=clamp_end(win_start,start); type silence; label 'silence detected'; detail 'observer silence ≥ threshold ({span}ms)'; field duration_ms. interruption end=clamp_end(start,start+500); type interruption; label 'interruption ({by})' by=spec.by or 'unknown'; detail=note.strip() or 'by={by}'; fields class(strip or None),by. sim.agent.audio_onset end=start+300; type audio_onset; label 'agent audio onset'; detail 'onset_frame={spec.onset_frame_idx} · vad={spec.vad.get(method,?)}'; field onset_frame_idx. sim.caller.audio_source_start end=start+300; type user_audio_source; label 'caller audio source'; detail 'provider={spec.provider or ?} · via={spec.via or ?}'. Recovery: agent_finals all transcript.agent.final audio-ms; for each barge point in order first agent final > barge_ms not consumed; end=clamp_end(recovery_ms,recovery_ms+800); type recovery; label 'agent recovery'; detail 'agent final after barge-in @ {barge_ms}ms'; field after_barge_ms. Final sort (start_ms,type_string) alphabetical on type.
6. tool_events.rs: _UNCLOSED_TOOL_TAIL_MS=500 _TOOL_BAND_MIN_MS=400 _TOOL_BAND_CAP_MS=400. Events tool.start/tool.end/tool.error. Pending key 'call:{call_id}' (call_id first of spec.call_id/spec.id) else 'evt:{event_id}'. name=first of spec.name/tool_name or 'tool'; arguments=first of spec.arguments/args/payload; call_id=first of spec.call_id/id. tool.start stores {call_id,name,start_ms,turn,source,arguments,parent_event_id,start_event_id}. End matching (1) call:{call_id} key (2) scan pending start_event_id==parent_event_id (3) len(pending)==1 take only one. dur=int(spec.duration_ms or 0); if dur<=0 and start_row dur=max(0,start-base_start). is_error=kind=='tool.error' or bool(spec.is_error). output=first of spec.output/result/error; error=first of spec.error/message if is_error. end_ms=base_start+max(400,min(dur,400)) if dur>0 else base_start+500 then clamp_end. Span fields call_id,name,start_ms,end_ms,duration_ms(None if dur<=0),turn,source,arguments,output,is_error,error,parent_event_id. Unclosed pending end=base+500 clamped duration_ms=None is_error=false output=None error=None. Sort (start_ms,name). _build_session_summary: session.usage->usage=dict(spec); session.agent_state->transitions {at_ms,from(str|None),to} appended only if new_state is not None; session.error->errors {at_ms,message=first of spec.message/error or 'session error'}. Returns None if all empty; else only non-empty keys {usage}/{state_transitions}/{errors}. _extract_chat_history last session.chat_history event reversed scan spec.items if list else None. _build_tool_summary tool_count from summary.tool_calls(int) else summary.metrics.tool_calls; tool_errors from summary.tool_errors else metrics.tool_errors; if <=0 from spans. Returns {tool_count,tool_errors} ints.
7. speech_origin.rs: _norm_speech keep only alnum+whitespace lowercase collapse. _CONTENT_STOP verbatim 39 words (Vietnamese + English stop words). _text_overlap(a,b) empty->false; len(shorter)>=5 && shorter in longer->true; content-word sets (len>=4 not in _CONTENT_STOP); empty intersection->false; any(len(w)>=5 for w in inter)->true; else len(inter)>=2. _mostly_script_say(text,say) all branches per Appendix A step 7. _tag_cues_with_markers marker m near cue c iff abs(m.ms-final_ms)<=8000 or abs(m.ms-start)<=1200 or (m.ms<=end && m.end_ms>=start) where final_ms=c.final_ms if not None else c.end. Non-user role->speech_origin='natural' no tagging. User scoring vs script markers (barge_in+script_cue): delta=final_ms-m.ms skip if delta<-800 or delta>15000. text_hit=_mostly_script_say(text,say) only if say non-empty and not starting '['. tiny=len(text.split())<=3 && len(text.strip())<=28. barge markers: text_hit && -500<=delta<=15000 accept score=100-min(40,max(0,delta)/400) integer div; tiny && 0<=delta<=3500 accept score=70-min(30,delta/200); else 0. non-barge accept=text_hit && 0<=delta<=8000 score=50. origin='script_barge' if barge else 'script_cue'. Best score wins. Time-only fallback: origin still natural len(text.split())<=2 && len(text.strip())<=24 -> first barge marker 0<=delta<=3500 -> script_barge. Late-STT fallback len(text.split())<=4; barge markers say non-empty not '[' _text_overlap(text,say) delta>=-500; key=(phrase,-abs(delta)) phrase=2 if nt in ns or ns in nt else 1; max key wins -> script_barge. _pin_script_window sets script_step_id,script_say,script_label; inject_ms=matched.start_ms or final_ms; audio_ms=matched.audio_ms or 0; if audio_ms<=0 2200 if origin=='script_barge' else 900. start_ms=max(0,inject_ms-80); end_ms=max(final_ms+500,inject_ms+audio_ms+350,existing end_ms); sets inject_ms. Full-line preference: if say non-empty not '[' len(text.strip())<len(say) len(text.split())<=6 -> stt_text=original text text=say. _synthetic_script_barge_cues: covered_steps (existing cues speech_origin in {script_barge,script_cue} and script_step_id) + covered_injects (their inject_ms). For each marker barge_in or type barge_in: skip if step_id in covered_steps; skip if any(abs(inject_ms-t)<600 for t in covered_injects). say=m.say strip; label=m.label or step_id or 'script barge'; display=say unless say starts '[' AND ends ']' -> label; strip leading '⚡'. audio_ms=m.audio_ms or 0; if <=0 max(1200,m.end_ms-inject_ms); end_ms=max(inject_ms+audio_ms+350,inject_ms+1200). Cue fields role 'user',start_ms=max(0,inject_ms-80),end_ms,final_ms=end_ms,text=display,speech_origin 'script_barge',script_step_id,script_say=say or display,script_label=label,inject_ms,synthetic:true,source:'sim.script',marker_tags:['barge_in']. Mark step + inject covered.
8. cues.rs payload assembly exact build order: load events/meta/summary -> duration (wav first else int(audio_meta['duration_ms']) TypeError/ValueError->None) -> t0 -> transcript cues -> tool spans -> markers -> _tag_cues_with_markers -> cues.extend(_synthetic_script_barge_cues) -> script_verify/assert_verify from summary fallback LAST script.verify/assert.verify event spec reversed scan -> behavior_summary summary.caller.behavior_summary (dict) -> summary.behavior_summary -> recompute script::build_caller_behavior_summary(events) -> observe_gaps meta.config_snapshot.observe_gaps -> config_snapshot.observe.observe_gaps -> []. marker_counts count per marker type. 9. report_server.rs port 8765: axum app + rust-embed static. Python ThreadingHTTPServer = one OS thread/connection; axum tokio::spawn-per-connection equivalent; keep server off CLI blocking ops (own runtime or Handle::spawn_blocking for cues regeneration; pipeline sync and cheap keep sync per request like Python). GET /api/runs/<id> and /api/runs/<id>/cues cues payload regenerated per request application/json;charset=utf-8 + Cache-Control no-store; 404 'run not found' if id empty or report dir missing; other second segment 404 'unknown api path'. title: Vendor gemini-live 0.1.8 + D4 fork patches (prereq P2)
description:
Vendor gemini-live 0.1.8 into crates/gemini-live and apply the D4 fork patches (prerequisite for P2 Gemini bridge). gemini-live is a real third-party dependency (jacoblincool/gemini-live-rs, MIT/Apache, ~1400 LOC core, stalled ~4 months) — it MUST be a crate in the workspace with its own Cargo.toml, not a module of lks. Sources verified at /tmp/glsrc/ (session.rs, transport.rs, config.rs, client_message.rs, server_message.rs, protocol.md).

PATCHES (confirmed against 0.1.8 source):
1. SpeechConfig.language_code (src/types/config.rs:56-60): add #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] pub language_code: Option<String>. The struct is already #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")] so it serializes languageCode. Keep optional so existing callers compile; mirrors python-genai SpeechConfig. NOTE: the patch goes on SpeechConfig, NOT VoiceConfig/PrebuiltVoiceConfig (corrects the research doc's earlier line).
2. Reconnect policy (src/session.rs:71-87): add pub reconnect_on_drop: bool (default false) to ReconnectPolicy. In the runner (session.rs:436-462) branch on the internal DisconnectReason (session.rs:408-414): GoAway -> always reconnect (inject resume handle, already done at session.rs:634-644); ConnectionLost -> reconnect only if reconnect_on_drop, else emit ServerEvent::Closed{reason} + set Closed status, mirroring Python caller (transport_dropped=True, no mid-call reconnect). The crate's default policy (auto-reconnect on both) is MORE aggressive than Python — do NOT ship it unpatched.
3. Surface close codes (src/transport.rs:311-324): patch RawFrame::Close to carry the close code (currently drops it, keeps only reason), enabling the Appendix D sec1.6 classification table (1006/1008/1011/1007).

VERIFY at P2 kickoff: ServerEvent::ModelAudio payload is 24 kHz raw PCM (INPUT_SAMPLE_RATE constant in session.rs); setup accepts inputAudioTranscription/outputAudioTranscription. Setup JSON emitted by the vendored crate is camelCase (realtimeInput, activityStart); Python sends snake_case (realtime_input); server accepts both — field presence matters, do NOT chase byte parity on key casing.

Do NOT rely on the crate for VAD/speech-started (ServerEvent has no speech-started/ended variants) — manual activity markers + TurnComplete/Interrupted is the contract, same as Python.

Fallback if the fork patch surface grows: hand-rolled tokio-tungstenite client (Candidate C, ~600-900 lines) mirroring R2's session/transport/config shape — the wire protocol is documented in protocol.md.

title: agent-sim-proto crate: prost AgentSessionMessage (prereq P3)

Parse or read error -> observer.error {where:'lk.agent.session', error}.

title: NEW_ARCHITECTURE_FOR_LKS_AND_LKSR: caller redesign implementation
description: Epic tracking the full caller-architecture rewrite from NEW_ARCHITECTURE_FOR_LKS_AND_LKSR.md (29 sections, research log + settled design). Goal: Behavior Contract locks WHAT, Orchestrator locks WHEN, AI Language Adapter (REQUIRED for do:) generates HOW as structured {act,target,slots,utterance}, Caller Contract Validator is the hard boundary before TTS/LiveKit, Interaction Planner handles delivery, sherpa-onnx TTS, LiveKit transport unchanged, Observer/Assertions/Report unchanged. Two absolute invariants: (1) no audio utterance reaches LiveKit without Validator VALID verdict; (2) every generated action carries behavior_id+turn_id+generation_id and stale actions never execute. Python lks is primary test bench (free rewrite of caller subsystem only), Rust lksr ports later against shared behavioral contract, no shared code. Source: NEW_ARCHITECTURE_FOR_LKS_AND_LKSR.md

title: P0-1 Caller Contract schema
description: Design and implement the canonical Caller Contract data model shared by lks Python and lksr Rust. Includes BehaviorContract with behavior/target/constraints using action-space not vocabulary-space, CandidateUtterance act/target/slots/utterance where claims are not evidence, ValidationResult verdicts VALID/INVALID/UNKNOWN/ERROR, ObservedAct model, and identity fields behavior_id/turn_id/generation_id/context_version. Acceptance: schema module with validation, unit tests, golden JSON fixtures reused by P0-2 and P0-8.
design: Place new code under src/livekit_agent_simulator/caller_contract/ (new subpackage; do NOT scatter contract types across existing modules). Keep every string in the contract generic: behavior names, targets, slots are caller-defined keys from scenario files, never hardcoded business vocabulary in src/ (AGENTS.md generic-core rule). Defaults portable: language en-US, timezone UTC in core. Design notes must list exact dataclasses/pydantic models: BehaviorContract, CandidateUtterance, ValidationResult, ObservedAct, GenerationIdentity. OWNER OF SHARED PRIMITIVES: this bead also defines the FailureReason enum (all 7 codes), the ended_by enum, and the shared is_current(identity, current_state) staleness helper used by validator, TTS publish, DTMF and control paths, so downstream beads import them instead of redefining. Include JSON Schema export for the golden fixtures so Rust can consume them without Python.
acceptance_criteria: pytest passes (uv run pytest -q). New tests file tests/test_caller_contract.py covers schema validation, UNKNOWN/ERROR mapping, generation-identity staleness predicate, and golden JSON fixtures under tests/fixtures/caller_contract/. title: P0-2a Caller Contract Validator deterministic layer
description: Deterministic checks of the validator pipeline: schema, act, target, slots, numeric constraints, forbidden facts, forbidden intents, goodbye-end control, lexical drift rules. Interface-first so the semantic backend bead can be swapped without moving the enforcement boundary. Rule: audio needs VALID verdict before TTS/LiveKit; invalid goes bounded retry then CALLER_BEHAVIOR_VIOLATION FAIL. Depends on the Caller Contract schema bead.
design: New subpackage src/livekit_agent_simulator/caller_contract/validator.py with a stable Validator interface class (validate(candidate, contract, observation) -> ValidationResult) so the semantic backend in .3 can be swapped without moving the enforcement boundary. The single enforcement choke point lives here: no other module may publish caller audio to LiveKit; document this with a code comment pointing at the two absolute invariants in the epic. Bounded retry N defaults to 2, configurable per behavior, then CALLER_BEHAVIOR_VIOLATION. All checks deterministic and dependency-free (stdlib only).
acceptance_criteria: pytest passes. tests/test_contract_validator.py covers: act mismatch reject, target mismatch reject, slot violation reject, forbidden-intent reject, end-call guard, lexical drift reject, valid pass, retry-then-fail path, and the canonical negotiate-price vs financing-drift vector. Each check is a separate test function with detailed logging on failure.
notes: [2026-09-10 05:00:07 UTC] Naming canonical (round-5 audit): validator returns ValidationResult with a verdict field; semantic layer returns ObservedAct. The enforcement choke point comment in code must reference epic invariant 1 using the exact phrase unvalidated utterance never reaches LiveKit so future greps find it.

title: P0-2b Semantic Intent Verification backend
description: Semantic layer: classify real utterance into observed act/target/slots via classification/entailment, not similarity alone. Must catch multi-act utterances and nested forbidden intents. UNKNOWN rejects, ERROR fails run. Precision over recall. Swappable backend behind P0-2a interface; no generator self-grading. Depends on P0-1 and P0-2a.
design: Backend interface SemanticVerifier with a single method classify(utterance, contract) -> ObservedAct plus confidence float. Implementations tried in order: (1) rule/lexical baseline, zero new deps; (2) local NLI/small model behind optional extra, never required for core tests; (3) LLM judge only as opt-in. Per AGENTS.md research loop: any new dependency needs a .venv proof before landing in src/. Generator claim is input only, never trusted: verifier re-derives observed act from utterance text alone. Multi-label output: primary act plus list of all detected acts for nested-forbidden-intent detection. Confidence threshold configurable, default conservative (precision over recall); below threshold yields UNKNOWN which the validator maps to reject. SCOPE LIMIT: no TTS or LiveKit code here; verifier is a pure function of text plus contract, so it stays unit-testable without audio or transport.
acceptance_criteria: pytest passes. tests/test_semantic_verifier.py covers: multi-act utterance reject, nested forbidden intent inside valid sentence reject, paraphrase-with-same-act accept, confidence-below-threshold rejects, backend-error maps to ERROR verdict. No new required dependency for the default path. Threshold value documented in code and docs.
close_reason: Implemented RuleBasedSemanticVerifier in caller_contract/semantic.py (tier 1 rule/lexical baseline of the layered plan): pure classify(utterance, contract) function with no candidate/self-grading, multi-label all_acts for multi-act and nested-forbidden-intent detection, confidence gating below SEMANTIC_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD (0.5, made public in validator.py). Validator's semantic block updated to reject low-confidence regardless of act match (unknown/ambiguous never valid). 13 new tests incl. multi-act, nested forbidden intent, paraphrase-accept, confidence-below-threshold, backend-error-to-ERROR. Full suite green (762 passed).

title: P0-3 Behavior DSL

Contract uses constraints with forbidden_intents and must_not. Optional interaction block for delivery config. Parser emits Behavior/CallerAction. say bypasses AI and validator but never bypasses Orchestrator turn gate. Constraint field names must match the BehaviorContract schema bead exactly; this parser imports field definitions from that bead, never redeclares them.
design: Extend the existing scenario parsing (scenario.py/script_parse.py) rather than a second parallel parser; add warnings for unknown keys instead of silent ignores. Behavior catalog is an allowlist loaded from scenario, not hardcoded business strings in src/ (generic-core rule). Keep JSONL compatibility: YAML-equivalent fields map onto existing Scenario model. Error messages must name the file, line, and field. NOTE: constraint field names validated here must match the BehaviorContract schema from .1 exactly; .4 imports field definitions from .1, never redeclares them.

title: P0-4 Orchestrator plus Turn Detector plus Behavior Evaluator
description: WHEN layer: Orchestrator state machine with turn/behavior/call timeout hierarchy, cancellation of stale jobs, barge-in ownership. Turn Detector converts LiveKit signals to TurnState with debounce and chunk correlation IDs. Behavior Evaluator separate from the caller validator beads with its own verdict enum SATISFIED/PARTIAL/NOT_SATISFIED. Enforce generation-identity staleness on every candidate and audio. Four-way agent-silence split. max_turns defaults to run FAIL. No LiveKit SDK injection. Depends on the Caller Contract schema bead and the Behavior DSL bead.
design: Extend run_orchestrator.py phased structure, do not fork a second orchestrator. Turn Detector is a new module under livekit/ consuming existing observer events only (no SDK injection, no new LiveKit dependency). Behavior Evaluator is a separate module from the caller validator in .2/.3 with its own verdict enum SATISFIED/PARTIAL/NOT_SATISFIED. Staleness check uses the shared is_current() helper from .1 at every publish site; .5 does not define its own versioning scheme. Barge-in execution lives here: Planner (.7) only emits trigger events. Timeouts: three explicit config keys with documented defaults. max_turns default behavior is run FAIL.

title: P0-5 AI Language Adapter
description: HOW layer REQUIRED for do steps: BehaviorContract plus structured ConversationContext plus agent observation in, structured CandidateUtterance out. One stateless Realtime call per adaptive turn; LKS owns state. say never calls AI. Provider and key in runtime config only. Backend failure retried then LANGUAGE_GENERATION_ERROR, never free-speech fallback. Depends on the Caller Contract schema bead, the Behavior DSL bead, and the Orchestrator bead.
design: New module under gemini/ or a new language/ package reusing existing provider clients; one call per adaptive turn with a hard per-call timeout and a bounded retry that ends in LANGUAGE_GENERATION_ERROR (code imported from .1, not redefined). Context builder function emits the minimal structured JSON (behavior, progress, agent_latest, relevant_facts, recent_turns capped at N). Provider/model from runtime config; credentials from target config.yaml only, never logged. Research loop required before touching provider wire formats: verify against installed packages in .venv.

title: P0-5b Caller Interaction Planner
description: DELIVERY layer after Validator PASS: deterministic interaction config pace/hesitation/stumble/pre_delay/backchannel; non-speech routes DTMF via LiveKit/SIP, silence as no audio, hangup as control. Whitelist semantic-preserving transforms only. Barge-in trigger only; execution stays with the Orchestrator bead. Depends on the Caller Contract schema bead, the Behavior DSL bead, and the Orchestrator bead.
design: New interaction/ module; backchannel/false-interrupt/noise reuse existing script-plumbing enums where they exist instead of inventing parallel ones. Transform whitelist enforced by construction: planner operates on token-level ops (insert_pause, repeat_fragment, pace_hint) that cannot introduce new semantic tokens; any code path adding free text is a design violation. title: Legacy caller (Gemini/OpenAI Script bridge) does not enforce verbatim say-line, causes audible non-stop/overlapping speech
description:
CONFIRMED via live run against voice-ai-agent (agent_fu6wozvzu41ztgo2rljs9zki, scenario ebroad-no-dtmf-intake-en, runs 002/003 in that target repo .agent-sim/reports/). User heard the LKS simulated caller talk continuously without respecting turn boundaries.

Evidence from events.jsonl (run 002): the exact same long transcript.user.final block (e.g. the callback-number line) is re-emitted verbatim as a NEW final event immediately before several subsequent script cues (postal_code, address, floors_and_units, no_other_questions, preferred_time), i.e. the simulated caller recaps/repeats prior answers instead of saying only the new scripted line.

Root cause (traced to source):
1. callers/gemini.py::script_speak_directive() instructs the Realtime model to speak the cue line 'verbatim, exactly once' -- this is a PROMPT-LEVEL instruction only, with no runtime enforcement. The model (OpenAI Realtime / Gemini Live) is free to ignore it and recap/expand, which the docstring itself acknowledges happened before ('Gemini paraphrase/expand the line').
2. callers/openai.py::_inject_openai_text() (~line 698-747) only waits for ANY audio to start queuing (mixer.speech_queued_ms() > 0) within a 2.8s deadline and returns True -- it never verifies the spoken content actually matches the injected line, nor truncates/cancels runaway speech that continues past the intended line.
3. livekit/observer.py::on_transcript() merge_as_same_turn logic (~line 511-559) then folds the recapped+new content into transcript events, which is why the SAME old block reappears as a fresh final right before each new cue -- an observer-side symptom of the caller-side content bug, not the root cause itself.
4. Script-step silence/turn triggers are not coordinated with in-flight caller audio still draining from a previous cue, so a new cue can fire while old speech is still playing -- audible as continuous, run-on talking with no turn gap.

This is exactly the hallucination class the new caller_contract/ redesign (NEW_ARCHITECTURE_FOR_LKS_AND_LKSR.md, all P0-1..P0-8 beads closed, ~350 tests) was built to eliminate via the Caller Contract Validator (hard boundary: unvalidated utterance never reaches transport) + Interaction Planner + Orchestrator turn gate + generation-staleness invariants. NONE of that new subsystem is wired into the live run path yet (run_orchestrator.py / callers/openai.py / callers/gemini.py / script_runner.py still run the old free-generation pipeline for real lks execute calls) -- confirmed by this bug reproducing on a live run today.

Fix direction (future work, out of scope for a quick patch): wire caller_contract.orchestrator/validator/interaction_planner into the actual Script execution path so that (a) the exact say-line is the ONLY audio ever published for a say/scripted cue (no live model generation involved for those, matching the say: primitive design), and (b) any adaptive/freeform caller turn goes through the Caller Contract Validator before publish. Until that integration lands, mitigate by: verifying _inject_openai_text's heard transcript actually matches the injected line (already have _inject_matches_say / _mostly_script_say helpers -- currently unused for hard enforcement) and cancelling/truncating extra audio once the match is confirmed, plus gating next-cue firing on the mixer being fully drained, not just on silence-timer elapsed.

title: Restore DTMF keypad support to the Python lks port
description:
Restore keypad (DTMF) support to the Python `lks` port, which lost it when
commit 665ec8c deleted the ScriptRunner engine on 2026-09-16.

Source of truth: docs/plans/PLAN-20260929-dtmf-python-restore.md (commit d431686).
This epic is deliberately SELF-CONTAINED. Do not need to read the plan doc.

THE DEFECT
`caller_steps` supports `- dtmf: "1"` in every layer except the last:
  - caller_contract/dsl.py:423-427  parse + validate          OK
  - caller_contract/interaction_planner.py:118  classify      OK but unwired
  - caller_contract/driver.py       EXECUTE                   MISSING
  - script/verify.py:268 + script/summary.py:16-21  report    already counts it
The driver enumerates five action.kind branches (say :358, do :445, wait :462,
play_audio :467, interrupt :546). dtmf and silence fall past all of them into
driver.py:592-593, which emits a generic contract.control event and returns
DriverResult(ended_by=SCENARIO). A documented authoring verb runs, reports
success, and does nothing.

WHY THIS IS A REGRESSION FIX, NOT A NEW FEATURE
lksr (Rust) still has the capability, having been ported before the Python
engine was deleted. But lksr ships no Windows release asset
(.github/workflows/rust-release.yml:31-33 states "lksr is Linux/macOS-only ...
Windows users: use Python lks"; install.ps1:122 throws). install.sh:10,24 and
install.ps1:21 both default to the Python binary, and pyproject.toml:33-34 marks
lks as the primary console script. Windows users therefore have no way to press
a key today.

DEMAND, VERIFIED AGAINST THE CONSUMER DATABASE
Flows live in the consumer's DB, not its repo, so a code search misses them.
Against voice-ai-backend's local `voice_ai_local` (postgresql://dev_user@localhost:5432):

  SELECT f."agentId", a.name, count(*) FROM "FlowNode" n
  JOIN "AgentFlow" f ON f.id = n."flowId"
  JOIN "Agent" a ON a.id = f."agentId"
  WHERE n.type = 'DTMF_INPUT' GROUP BY 1, 2;

  agent_g9srhevzdanmpue372yfgzi7 | イーブロード                      | 1
  agent_w3ph2c35kisb1ibqythi571j | イーブロード (3-Cụm Macro-Node) | 1

agent_w3ph2c35kisb1ibqythi571j has a DTMF_INPUT node (id
xr617az7554nbwvkndfe86ro) with dtmfMode=single_key, acceptedKeys=["1","2","3"],
minDigits=maxDigits=1, outputVariableName=dtmf_value, overallTimeoutMs=15000,
interDigitTimeoutMs=4000, maxRetries=2, failureAction=switch_voice, and four
DTMF-triggered FlowTransition rows routing on {{dtmf_value}} == "1" | "2" |
"3" plus a dtmf_timeout handle to a Timeout node.

WHAT IS *NOT* EVIDENCE
Archived runs 058/063 show error: null in events.jsonl. Those prove an FFI
round-trip completed, and both ran in webrtc_sim, the one caller mode where the
sim and agent share a room. They are not delivery evidence.

THE ARCHITECTURAL CONSTRAINT THAT SHAPES EVERYTHING
publish_dtmf sends a PublishSipDtmfRequest data packet
(livekit/rtc/participant.py:302-316). The Python API exposes no destination
identities, so it is always a room broadcast. SimLegHandle
(livekit/sim_leg/protocol.py:24-32) carries TWO rooms and
run_orchestrator.py:366 builds the caller bridge with room=leg_handle.sim_room.

  mode                     sim_room           agent_room        shared
  webrtc_sim               dispatch.room_name dispatch.room_name  yes
  outbound_human_pickup    agent_room_name    dispatch.room_name  yes
  inbound_sip              lks-sip-{run_id}   resolved, separate  NO
  outbound_sim_callee      lks-sip-{run_id}   room_name_for_run   NO
  agent_dials              lks-sip-{run_id}   room_name_for_run   NO

Publishing from the sim room reaches nobody in the last three modes. Publishing
from the agent room (Observer holds it, observer.py:96) is equally wrong: the
observer connects as lks-obs-{run_id[:8]} and voice-ai-agent drops any sender
that is not its first remote participant
(voice-ai-agent/src/session/attach-flow-runtime.ts:729, with
getCallerIdentity() at attach-room-participant.ts:39-40). Correct room, wrong
sender. The fix is a fail-fast gate, not a choice between two publishers.

SCOPE OF THIS EPIC
One new module, one driver branch, one dsl relaxation, one shipped template,
one warning fix, doc updates, tests, and the paired Rust change. No new
authoring syntax, no config knob, no CLI flag, no MCP tool. See each child bead
for detail.

Definition of done: every child closed, full Python suite green at the
baseline-plus-delta count, cargo test --workspace green, the three decisions in
this epic recorded with their answers.
notes:
[2026-09-29 03:27:18 UTC] [2026-09-29 POLISH ROUND 5] HISTORICAL LINEAGE. This epic is NOT greenfield and
must not be presented as one. Found by searching the bead DB, which holds 123
issues (97 closed) that `br list` does not show.

- livekit-agent-simulator-b7a "P1.A DTMF / IVR Script action + events + asserts"
  was shipped and closed on 2026-07-14. Its close reason reads: "DRAFT shipped:
  action=dtmf + publish_dtmf + sim.dtmf + Assert.sip.dtmf_sequence +
  ivr-pin-entry-draft.jsonl. Unit tests 34 pass. NO real E2E merge to main until
  worker handles SIP DTMF (only press-digit spoken). Branch
  feat/p1a-dtmf-script-draft."

  So the capability was deliberately shipped as a DRAFT with a real-E2E waiver,
  on the script: path, not caller_steps:.

- 665ec8c (2026-09-16) deleted script/runtime.py, which contained that work,
  as "dead code: 0 instantiations outside its own tests".

  That is the regression this epic fixes. When citing the regression, name 665ec8c
  as the deleting commit and b7a as the original delivery. Both are verifiable
  in this tracker and in git.

- The Rust port kept its copy, which is why lksr still works.

TIMING, NOW SETTLED AGAINST THE SOURCE
b7a's description says "w=pause (~0.5s)". That was an aspirational July design
note, NOT what shipped. Verified against the deleted implementation
(`git show 665ec8c^:src/livekit_agent_simulator/script/runtime.py`):

    line 294:  kind = "sim.script.dtmf"
    line 308:  await asyncio.sleep(0.12)              # the 'w' pause
    line 311:  await local.publish_dtmf(code=DMAP[ch], digit=ch)
    line 315:  await asyncio.sleep(0.15)              # gap after each tone

So 120 ms and 150 ms are the real historical values, and the Rust port
faithfully carried them (lks-livekit/src/callers/openai.rs). Do not "correct"
them to 500 ms on the strength of the old bead text.

EVENT NAME EVOLVED
b7a shipped it as `sim.dtmf`. The tree now uses `sim.script.dtmf`. This epic
emits the current name; see the event-name bead for why reusing it is what makes
script/summary.py and script/verify.py live readers with no new code.

RELATIONSHIPS ADDED
b7a and the two Behavior-DSL beads (otd.4 P0-3, otd.7 P0-5b) are linked as
`related` so this epic is traceable from the work that preceded it.
---
[2026-09-29 03:27:50 UTC] [2026-09-29 POLISH ROUND 6] WIP.md ASSERTS A CAPABILITY THAT DOES NOT EXIST.
This is very likely why the regression went unnoticed.

WIP.md's competitive snapshot is
    | Capability | lks | Hamming / Coval / Cekura | LiveKit pytest |
and its DTMF row (WIP.md:51) reads
    | DTMF / IVR scripting | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ |

so the repo's own document claims `lks` HAS DTMF / IVR scripting. It does not,
in the Python port. 665ec8c removed the execution path on 2026-09-16 and the
claim was never updated.

WIP.md:94 is worse, because it is the roadmap table and marks the work finished:
    | **P1.A** | **DTMF / IVR scripting** ✅ | Feature + E2E logic |
    Done: Script action dtmf ("1234#", w=pause); publish_dtmf;
    sim.script.dtmf events; assert sequence; templates ivr-pin-entry | C2 / F1 / L3 |

Every item in that "Done" cell is true of the July 2026 b7a delivery and false
of the tree today, except the pieces that survived in the parser and the
reporter (script/models.py SUPPORTED_ACTIONS, script/verify.py, script/summary.py).
There is no execution path. "Done" plus a table claiming parity is exactly the
signal that stopped anyone asking the question.

THE LESSON IS THE POINT, NOT THE TYPO
The failure was not a stale checkbox. It was that no artifact asserted the claim.
WIP.md said done, the tracker said done, the templates shipped, the reporting
counted the event kind -- and nothing anywhere executed a tone. The whole DTMF
restore exists to produce the artifact WIP.md was implicitly relying on: a test
that drives the shipped template through the real driver and asserts the event.

Do not simply flip the WIP.md cells to ❌. Marking it ❌ records the current
truth but leaves nothing to prevent the same drift. The tripwire bead is the
durable fix; WIP.md should cite it.
---
[2026-09-29 05:07:00 UTC] BASELINE (measured on the Windows dev box, .venv pytest, 2026-09-29) after the c0d3e26 mutant revert (commit eda4216): 1156 passed, 2 skipped, 2 xfailed, 0 failed. The pre-revert count is the same triple - the mutants were invisible to the suite, so this number is a floor, not evidence of correctness. Later beads must show a DELTA from 1156 to prove they changed what they intended; a bead that still reports exactly 1156/2/2 probably added no assertion.
