title: Decision: shared-room-only DTMF, or authorise PSTN plumbing
description:
DECISION BEAD. Record the answer with br update --notes-push, then close.

THE QUESTION
The restore makes DTMF work only where the sim and the agent share one LiveKit
room: webrtc_sim and outbound_human_pickup. In inbound_sip, outbound_sim_callee
and agent_dials they are separate rooms and a data packet cannot cross.

Real DTMF is a PSTN use case, and PSTN is exactly the topology this refuses.
The restore therefore ships a fail-fast gate, which makes the gap LOUD but does
not CLOSE it. Someone has to decide whether that is acceptable.

OPTIONS
(a) Accept shared-room-only for now. Recommended. Ship the gate, file a bead
    for the real plumbing. Rationale: the two-room case needs server-side or
    SIP-leg work, not a client change, and no current consumer flow requires it.
(b) Authorise real plumbing: a dedicated participant in the agent room that
    the agent perceives as the caller. This is the correct long-term fix and is
    a materially larger change touching SimLegHandle and the SIP legs.
(c) Ask voice-ai-agent to relax the sender filter at
    src/session/attach-flow-runtime.ts:729 to accept any sender. Cheapest, but
    it moves the correctness burden onto the consumer and weakens their agent.

RECOMMENDATION: (a), plus beads for (b) and (c).

DO NOT let the fail-fast read as "done". The gate turning a silent no-op into a
loud error is a correctness win, not delivery of PSTN DTMF.

BLOCKS the room-gate implementation bead, because option (b) changes what the
gate builds.
notes: [2026-09-29 05:44:08 UTC] NEW EVIDENCE before this decision is closed — the sip_dtmf_received lead, and it cuts BOTH ways. Read this before choosing an option; it may make (c) unnecessary and it may add a fourth option. (a) client-side DTMF is a first-class SDK surface, not something LKS has to invent. Verified in the installed SDK (livekit 1.1.13): LocalParticipant.publish_dtmf(*, code: int, digit: str) at livekit/rtc/participant.py:302; SipDTMF dataclass at room.py:139 (exported rtc/__init__.py:72,177); sip_dtmf_received in EventTypes at room.py:78, documented at room.py:403, emitted at room.py:1019-1025 carrying SipDTMF(code, digit, participant). The wire form is PublishSipDtmfRequest{code, digit, destination_identities}, and the FFI delivers inbound tones as DataPacketReceivedH.sip_dtmf. LiveKit docs (https://docs.livekit.io/telephony/features/dtmf/): 'Any participant in the room can use the publishDtmf API to transmit DTMF tones to the room. SIP participants in the room receive the tones and relay them to the telephone user.' Underlying transport is RTP telephone-event/8000 (RFC 4733), not a data topic. WHAT THIS DOES NOT FIX: both publish_dtmf and sip_dtmf_received are room-scoped, so the sim/agent room split stands unchanged. Option (c) may still be moot for a different reason though: when a real PSTN caller presses a digit, the SIP leg relays it into ITS room and every participant there gets a native sip_dtmf_received with participant set to the SIP participant. If the agent is in that room it can subscribe natively, with no LKS relay and therefore no sender filter to relax. Whether that is true depends on which room the SIP participant joins, which I have NOT verified — do not treat it as settled. THE INVERSION, and the reason to re-read option (a): the plan's line 'In the three two-room modes, publishing from the sim room reaches the observer and nothing else' is true about the AGENT and incomplete about the SIP leg. Per the topology table, all three two-room modes put sim_room at lks-sip-{run_id} — that is the SIP room, which is where the SIP participant lives. So for the sim-as-IVR-caller flow (the dtmf-ivr-menu template, 3tv.5.1) the sim is co-located with exactly the participant that relays tones to the real phone. The room split that blocks sim->agent may be what ENABLES sim->IVR. That would make option (b) (a dedicated participant in the agent room) the wrong shape for the IVR case even where it is right for the agent-facing case. NOT VERIFIED IN PRACTICE — this is read off the topology table and the SDK surface, not off a run. Before it changes the decision, someone should confirm by one live call that publish_dtmf from the sim actually produces a tone on the far-end phone in outbound_sim_callee. If it does, the fail-fast gate should distinguish 'no publisher because the agent is unreachable' from 'tones go to the PSTN leg fine' rather than reporting both as TRANSPORT_ERROR. Filed by the peer session's turn-alignment research; no code touched.

title: Decision: align script_cues_fired across Python and Rust
description:
DECISION BEAD. Record the answer with br update --notes-push, then close.

THE QUESTION
Python and Rust disagree on a machine-readable summary.json field today.

  Python  script/summary.py:16-21  script_action_kinds = {
            sim.script.cue, sim.script.dtmf, sim.script.wait, sim.script.hang_up }
  Rust    lks-core/src/script/summary.rs:23-26  filters on sim.script.cue only

So the same scenario reports script_cues_fired: 1 under lks and 0 under lksr.
This predates the DTMF restore. The restore makes it VISIBLE rather than hidden,
because the contract path will now emit sim.script.dtmf, which Python counts and
Rust ignores.

OPTIONS
(a) Align Rust up to the four-kind set. Matches Python, and matches what the
    plan's event-name decision assumes.
(b) Align Python down to sim.script.cue. Smaller diff in Rust, but throws away
    the DTMF/wait/hang_up counting that script/summary.py:14-15 was written for.

RECOMMENDATION: (a). The Python set is the deliberate one, documented in the
comment at summary.py:14-15 ("a pure-DTMF run must not report 0 cues fired").

This is deliberately NOT part of the DTMF restore commit. It is a separate small
PR so the restore diff stays reviewable.

BLOCKS the Rust summary-alignment bead only.

title: Foundation: publisher module, driver branch, room gate, dsl trigger
description:
Sub-epic for the four code changes that make DTMF actually reach LiveKit from
the Python port. Everything here is offline-testable; none of it touches the
web player, the report format, or any CLI/MCP surface.

Children, in dependency order:
  1. dtmf-module         new caller_contract/dtmf.py (the wire seam)
  2. dtmf-driver-branch  the dtmf branch in the contract driver
  3. dtmf-room-gate      live_wiring construction + fail-fast room gate
  4. dtmf-dsl-trigger    allow trigger: on a dtmf step

(1) blocks (2) and (3). (4) is independent of the wire and can land in parallel.

WHY A SEAM AND NOT A DIRECT CALL
The driver already receives injected collaborators (assets at driver.py:213-215,
the emit callable, the agent-turn waiter). The repository's idiom for a small
capability is a narrow Protocol plus one concrete implementation, injected
side-by-side with the existing seams (see live_wiring.py:460,497). Do NOT add a
publish_dtmf method to the CallersBridge or PublishSink Protocol: that trades a
mechanical test edit for optional-hook dead surface, which is precisely the
shape commit 665ec8c deleted from the tree.

HARD RULE FOR ALL FOUR CHILDREN
AGENTS.md "Product rule: no dead features" and "no dead features" are the
governing constraints. Every line here must be reachable from the shipped
template. If you cannot name the call path, do not write the line.

title: New module caller_contract/dtmf.py: DtmfPublisher seam and RoomDtmfPublisher
description:
Create src/livekit_agent_simulator/caller_contract/dtmf.py. This is the only
wire call the restore adds, and the only place that knows LiveKit's DTMF code
map.

API TO BUILD

  DTMF_PAUSE_MS   = 120    # 'w' pause
  DTMF_GAP_MS     = 150    # gap after each published tone
  PUBLISH_TIMEOUT_S = 5.0

  DTMF_CODES = {"0":0, ..., "9":9, "*":10, "#":11}

  @dataclass(frozen=True)
  class DtmfResult:
      digits: str
      published: int
      error: str | None

  class DtmfPublisher(Protocol):
      async def publish(self, digits: str) -> DtmfResult: ...

  class RoomDtmfPublisher:
      def __init__(self, participant: rtc.LocalParticipant) -> None: ...
      async def publish(self, digits: str) -> DtmfResult: ...

RoomDtmfPublisher.publish walks the string left to right:
  - 'w'      -> await asyncio.sleep(DTMF_PAUSE_MS / 1000); continue
  - mapped   -> publish, then await asyncio.sleep(DTMF_GAP_MS / 1000)
  - unknown  -> error = f"unknown DTMF char {ch!r}"; break
  - any exception, including asyncio.TimeoutError -> capture into error; break

THE wait_for WRAPPER IS MANDATORY, NOT DEFENSIVE
livekit's Queue overrides asyncio.Queue.wait_for at
livekit/rtc/_utils.py:103 and DROPS the timeout parameter. publish_dtmf awaits
that queue with no cancel path (livekit/rtc/participant.py:320-328). So:

    await asyncio.wait_for(participant.publish_dtmf(code=..., digit=ch),
                           PUBLISH_TIMEOUT_S)

Without the wrapper, a dead transport hangs the driver forever. Worse, it hangs
it silently: _on_hold_timeout calls bridge.sim_hang_up(), which does not cancel
the driver task, so the `finally: bridge.stop()` at
run_orchestrator.py:430-431 never runs and the run never finalizes. Bounded is
the difference between a failed run and a wedged process. The test file must
cover this (dtmf-tests case 3).

DTMF_CODES IS LIVEKIT'S MAP, NOT RFC 4733
  LiveKit: "0"-"9" -> 0-9, "*" -> 10, "#" -> 11
  RFC 4733: same digits, but "*" -> 10, "#" -> 15
A real SIP caller pressing '#' produces code 15; livekit/sip ignores `code` on
the room-to-phone leg, so the divergence is invisible in a real call but can
surface in an agent that asserts on SipDTMF.code rather than .digit. Document
this in the module docstring. Do NOT "fix" the map.

DOCSTRING MUST ALSO STATE WHAT THE EVENT PROVES
A sim.script.dtmf event proves the tones were SUBMITTED TO THE LOCAL
PARTICIPANT. It does not prove an agent received them. The server excludes the
sender from data fan-out, so the sim structurally cannot observe its own tone.
The only in-repo delivery evidence is the agent's own reaction, e.g.
demo/dtmf-feature/agent/dtmf_agent.py:120.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- Module imports cleanly; no import-time dependency on a live room.
- A fake participant recording calls shows "1w2#" -> [(1,"1"), (2,"2"),
  (11,"#")] and 'w' produces no call.
- A fake whose publish_dtmf awaits forever returns DtmfResult(error=...) within
  PUBLISH_TIMEOUT_S rather than hanging.
- Docstring covers the code-map divergence and the delivery-evidence caveat.
notes:
[2026-09-29 03:26:27 UTC] [2026-09-29 POLISH ROUND 4] Interface notes confirmed against the tree.

- RoomDtmfPublisher takes a `livekit.rtc.LocalParticipant`, NOT a `Room`.
  The room is resolved and gated in live_wiring; the publisher only ever calls
  participant.publish_dtmf(code=, digit=) at livekit/rtc/participant.py:302.
  Keeping the room out of the publisher means the unit tests need only a
  one-method fake participant, not a room stand-in.

- Because of that, dtmf.py should NOT import anything from
  caller_contract/__init__.py. It imports livekit.rtc for the type only. This
  keeps it importable in tests without a LiveKit connection.

- DtmfResult is frozen and has exactly three fields: digits, published, error.
  The driver emits all three into the event spec, so no field may be dropped
  and none may be added without updating the event contract in
  script/summary.py:16-21 and script/verify.py:268.

title: Add the dtmf branch to ContractCallerDriver and close the silent fall-through
description:
This is the bead that actually fixes the defect.

CURRENT STATE
caller_contract/driver.py dispatches five action kinds explicitly:
  say :358, do :445, wait :462, play_audio :467, interrupt :546
Everything else lands at driver.py:592-593:

    # dtmf / silence: control actions, never AI/TTS.
    _emit("contract.control", {"kind": action.kind, "line": action.line_no})

`silence` is correct there. `dtmf` is the bug: a documented verb that parses,
runs, and returns DriverResult(ended_by=SCENARIO) having done nothing.

WHAT TO BUILD
Add an explicit `dtmf` branch with the other control branches, after
play_audio (:467):

  1. Gate on trigger, reusing the existing _wait_trigger (driver.py:1239) the
     same way say and play_audio do. If the trigger does not fire, continue.
     (This depends on dtmf-dsl-trigger lifting the dsl restriction; if that
     bead has not landed, gate the branch but expect no dtmf step can carry a
     trigger yet.)
  2. result = await self.dtmf.publish(action.dtmf_digits or "")
  3. Emit sim.script.dtmf with spec {digits, published, error}.
  4. If published == 0 and result.error is not None:
     return self._fail(FailureReason.TRANSPORT_ERROR,
                       f"dtmf publish failed: {result.error}",
                       EndedBy.TRANSPORT, completed, spoken)
  5. `silence` keeps emitting contract.control unchanged.

Inject the publisher as a run() keyword beside `assets`
(driver.py:213-215), matching the sibling seam at live_wiring.py:460,497. Not
a dataclass field.

EVENT NAME: sim.script.dtmf, NOT contract.dtmf
Three reasons, strongest first:
  - Reusing the existing vocabulary means script/summary.py:16-21 already counts
    it, and build_caller_behavior_summary runs unconditionally, so dtmf_fired
    and script_cues_fired come alive with no new reader.
  - run_orchestrator.py:565-568 skips script_verify for contract scenarios
    regardless of which kinds are emitted, so "the contract path must use
    contract.* vocabulary" is not actually true.
  - The Rust port's contract path already emits sim.script.dtmf
    (lks-livekit/src/script.rs:534) for the same authored step. Same scenario,
    same event name, both ports.
A bespoke contract.dtmf kind would be read by nothing. That is a dead feature.

CLOSE THE FALL-THROUGH (the durable part of this bead)
The bare fall-through is exactly the shape that let a known verb become a
no-op. After handling dtmf and silence, make anything else fail loudly:

    return self._fail(FailureReason.VALIDATION_ERROR,
                      f"unhandled caller action {action.kind!r}",
                      EndedBy.ERROR, completed, spoken)

Then the next addition to _KNOWN_ACTION_KINDS fails loudly instead of silently.
This is the specific tripwire commit 665ec8c lacked.

A TEST CURRENTLY PINS THE BUG
tests/test_contract_live_wiring.py:685 test_wait_and_dtmf_never_publish asserts
urlopen was never called for [{wait:10},{dtmf:"123"},{end:true}]. Its wait half
is right; its dtmf half encodes the defect. Rename to test_wait_never_publish,
keep the wait half, move the dtmf half to the new test file. See dtmf-tests.

DO NOT add a writer field to the publisher. The driver already emits the full
result. BridgePublishSink.writer is load-bearing (publish_sink.py:63,79); a
publisher's would not be.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- A dtmf step publishes tones and emits exactly one sim.script.dtmf.
- dtmf publishes NO PCM (regression 764dc3a; asserted in the new test file).
- An unknown handler kind returns VALIDATION_ERROR instead of falling through.
- silence behaviour is unchanged.
notes:
[2026-09-29 03:25:25 UTC] [2026-09-29 POLISH ROUND 3] TWO CORRECTIONS, both from reading the code rather
than trusting the earlier draft. The second one matters more.

1. _wait_trigger IS MODULE-LEVEL, NOT A METHOD.
   Defined at caller_contract/driver.py:1239 as a plain async function. Call it
   as `_wait_trigger(action.trigger, agent, emit=_emit)` -- the same call shape
   used at :381 (say) and :482 (play_audio). There is no `self._wait_trigger`.

2. A TRIGGER THAT NEVER FIRES MUST FAIL, NOT `continue`.
   This bead previously said "if the trigger does not fire, continue". That is
   WRONG and it reintroduces the exact defect this epic exists to remove: a
   keypress that silently never happens, reported as a clean run.

   Both existing callers fail instead. play_audio at driver.py:482-494:

       fired = await _wait_trigger(action.trigger, agent, emit=_emit)
       if not fired:
           _emit("contract.behavior_violation",
                 {"reason": "TRIGGER_TIMEOUT", "line": action.line_no})
           return self._fail(
               FailureReason.BEHAVIOR_TIMEOUT,
               f"trigger {action.trigger.kind!r} never fired",
               EndedBy.TIMEOUT, completed, spoken,
           )

   say at :381 does the same. The dtmf branch must match. A dtmf step whose
   trigger times out is a failed scenario, because the caller pressed nothing.

3. THERE IS AN EXISTING IDIOM FOR "REQUIRED DEPENDENCY MISSING".
   play_audio, immediately below the above at :495-500:

       if player is None or getattr(player, "play_asset", None) is None:
           return self._fail(
               FailureReason.TRANSPORT_ERROR,
               "play_audio requires an AudioAssetPlayer (no silent drop)",
               EndedBy.TRANSPORT, completed, spoken,
           )

   Use this shape verbatim for the missing publisher in the room-gate case, with
   a message that names the two-room topology. Matching the house style rather
   than inventing a new one is what makes this read as the same codebase, and
   "(no silent drop)" is the established statement of the principle this whole
   epic is enforcing.

4. _fail SIGNATURE, for exactness: _fail(self, reason, detail, ended_by,
   completed, spoken) at driver.py:1140. It returns a DriverResult, so the
   branch must `return self._fail(...)`, not call it bare.
---
[2026-09-29 03:26:26 UTC] [2026-09-29 POLISH ROUND 4] THE PUBLISHER IS A LOCAL, NOT self.dtmf.
Earlier drafts of this bead said "inject as a run() keyword beside assets" and
then referred to it as `self.dtmf`. Those two statements disagree, and the
second one is wrong.

`assets` is NEVER stored on the driver. It flows as a plain keyword-only
parameter through three frames:

  run()            assets: AudioAssetPlayer | None = None      driver.py:213
    -> _run_actions call                                    driver.py:284  (assets=assets)
      -> _run_actions param  assets: AudioAssetPlayer | None driver.py:346
        -> read as a local  player = assets                  driver.py:495

Follow exactly that shape:

  run(..., dtmf: DtmfPublisher | None = None)               # keyword-only
    -> _run_actions call          dtmf=dtmf                 # at the :284 site
      -> _run_actions param        dtmf: DtmfPublisher | None
        -> read as a local in the dtmf branch

There is no self.dtmf, and there should not be. The driver holds no per-run
state for collaborators; anything it keeps would leak across runs, and these
driver objects are constructed per run in live_wiring.py:347.

_nothing_else_needs_changing_: no dataclass field, no __init__ change, no
Constructor wiring beyond the single call site.
---
[2026-09-29 03:27:18 UTC] [2026-09-29 POLISH ROUND 5] CROSS-PORT EVENT SPEC DIVERGENCE, DECIDED NOT TO
HIDE. Recorded here because the two ports emit the same event NAME with
different spec KEYS.

Rust (lks-livekit/src/script.rs:528-543) emits:
    { "step_id": <script step id>, "digits": <string> }

The contract path has no step_id. CallerAction identifies an action by `line_no`
(caller_contract/dsl.py:171, "one of _KNOWN_ACTION_KINDS" is kind; line_no is
the source position). So the Python contract-path event should be:

    { "digits": <string>, "published": <int>, "error": <string|null>, "line_no": <int> }

ACCEPT THE DIVERGENCE, DO NOT CLOSE IT HERE
`digits` is the only field any consumer reads, and both ports carry it under the
same key. Everything past that is diagnostic. script/summary.py:16-21 and
script/verify.py:268 count events by KIND, not by spec fields, so no reader
breaks.

What would break: any future reader that assumes `step_id` is always present.
That is precisely why the docs bead requires the delivery-evidence caveat, and
why `line_no` belongs in the Python spec rather than being omitted. Omit it and
the two ports' events look interchangeable when they are not.

A Rust change to emit the same four keys would need the projection in
lks-core/src/scenario.rs:805-808 to carry `line_no` through. Out of scope here.
If someone wants true spec parity, file it as a separate bead rather than
widening this one.

title: Allow trigger: on a dtmf step in caller_contract/dsl.py
description:
caller_contract/dsl.py:415-422 currently rejects trigger and barge_in for
dtmf and wait alike:

    if kind in ("dtmf", "wait"):
        if "trigger" in raw_step or "barge_in" in raw_step:
            raise _err("trigger:/barge_in: are only supported on say: steps "
                       "in this slice", ...)

The error message already contradicts the code, which supports trigger on
play_audio. This bead lifts dtmf out of that reject tuple. It is a two-line
deletion.

WHY IT MATTERS
CallerAction already carries `trigger` (dsl.py:166) and _wait_trigger already
exists (driver.py:1239) and already serves both say and play_audio. Nothing
structural blocks dtmf from using it.

More concretely: this preserves the only historical behaviour that made DTMF
work. demo/dtmf-feature/.agent-sim/reports/058-press-4-*/events.jsonl ran
`trigger: agent_speaking`. Without trigger support the tone fires at t=0,
before the agent has read its menu prompt, and the demo reads as broken. With
it, the caller presses after the agent starts talking, which is how a human
uses a phone.

SCOPE — do NOT lift `wait`
Leave wait in the reject tuple. This bead is about dtmf only. Widening the
surface for wait is scope creep and nobody asked for it.

DO NOT touch barge_in here
barge_in has no meaning for a keypress (there is no caller speech to cut
across). Leave it rejected; only lift the trigger check.

DEPENDENCY NOTE
This is independent of the wire. It can land in parallel with dtmf-module and
does not need the publisher to exist. But it is only USEFUL once
dtmf-driver-branch consumes the trigger, so if you land it alone the feature is
still inert and the no-dead-features rule is not satisfied yet. Land it with or
immediately after the driver branch.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- parse_step({"dtmf": "1", "trigger": {...}}) no longer raises.
- parse_step({"wait": 5, "trigger": {...}}) STILL raises (regression guard).
- parse_step({"dtmf": "1", "barge_in": True}) STILL raises (regression guard).
- The error string for wait no longer claims to be about say steps only, or is
  narrowed accordingly.

title: Construct the publisher in live_wiring with a fail-fast room-identity gate
description:
This is the bead the whole design turns on. A research panel's highest-scoring
proposal published from bridge.room; a later review found that room is the SIM
room, and in 3 of 5 caller modes it does not contain the agent. Read this bead
before writing any wiring code.

WHY BOTH OBVIOUS PUBLISHERS ARE WRONG

SimLegHandle (livekit/sim_leg/protocol.py:24-32) carries two rooms:
  agent_room, agent_room_name, sim_room, sim_room_name, sim_identity,
  agent_identity, mode
run_orchestrator.py:366 builds the caller bridge with room=leg_handle.sim_room.

publish_dtmf sends a PublishSipDtmfRequest data packet
(livekit/rtc/participant.py:302-316). The Python API exposes no destination
identities, so it is always a room broadcast. Per mode:

  mode                  sim_room          agent_room       shared
  webrtc_sim            dispatch.room     dispatch.room    yes
  outbound_human_pickup agent_room_name   dispatch.room    yes
  inbound_sip           lks-sip-{run_id}  resolved, sep.   NO
  outbound_sim_callee   lks-sip-{run_id}  room_name_for_run NO
  agent_dials           lks-sip-{run_id}  room_name_for_run NO

Anchors: webrtc.py:40-41, human_pickup.py:159, inbound.py:36-37,158,197-198,
sim_callee.py:34-35, agent_dials.py:18-19.

Publishing from the sim room in the last three modes reaches the observer and
nobody else. It would emit a green sim.script.dtmf for a tone that reached
nobody, which is worse than the current silent no-op because it looks like proof.

Publishing from the agent room instead is equally wrong. Observer does hold it
(observer.py:96 self.room = room; built at run_orchestrator.py:333) and
observer is already positional arg 3 of run_contract_driver_path
(live_wiring.py:302). But the observer connects as lks-obs-{run_id[:8]}
(inbound.py:183, agent_dials.py:63, sim_callee.py:87), and the live consumer
filters on sender identity:

  // voice-ai-agent/src/session/attach-flow-runtime.ts:729
  if (participant.identity !== options.getCallerIdentity()) return;

getCallerIdentity() returns the FIRST remote participant
(attach-room-participant.ts:39-40), which in inbound_sip is deterministically
the SIP participant, awaited at inbound.py:141-150 BEFORE the observer joins at
:183. So observer-room DTMF is dropped silently. Right room, wrong sender.

(The in-repo demo agent at demo/dtmf-feature/agent/dtmf_agent.py:120 does NOT
filter, which is why the historical runs appeared to work. Do not treat the
demo as evidence that observer publishing is viable.)

WHAT TO BUILD
In run_contract_driver_path, build the publisher ABOVE the driver constructor
at live_wiring.py:347. Do not put it beside the sink at :362; the constructor
runs first.

    # A tone must be published by the participant the agent perceives as the
    # caller, which requires one shared room. In the SIP legs the sim and the
    # agent sit in different LiveKit rooms and a data packet cannot cross.
    _shared = (getattr(bridge, "room", None) is not None
               and bridge.room.name == observer.room.name)
    dtmf_pub = (RoomDtmfPublisher(bridge.room.local_participant)
                if _shared else None)

When _shared is false the driver has no publisher, and the dtmf branch fails
with FailureReason.TRANSPORT_ERROR and a message that NAMES THE TWO-ROOM
TOPOLOGY. Fail-fast, not a silent stub. AGENTS.md forbids half-implemented
backends, and a stub that no-ops would reintroduce the exact defect this epic
removes.

TWO TRAPS THAT WILL BITE OTHERWISE

1. Access room.local_participant DIRECTLY. Do not write
   getattr(room, "local_participant", None). The property raises a bare
   Exception("cannot access local participant before connecting")
   (livekit/rtc/room.py:224), and getattr does NOT swallow a raised exception
   from a property. Your safety net would itself raise.

2. Declare `room: rtc.Room` on the CallerBridge Protocol (callers/base.py) so
   .room is in-contract rather than duck-typed. Without it, the gate's
   getattr(bridge, "room", None) is always-None-by-accident and every mode
   silently fails closed.

BLOCKED BY
dtmf-decision-two-room. If that decision chooses option (b) (authorise real
PSTN plumbing), the shape of what gets built here changes. Check it first.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- Shared room (webrtc_sim): publisher constructed, tones publish.
- Split room (inbound_sip): publisher is None, a dtmf step fails with
  TRANSPORT_ERROR and a message naming the two-room topology.
- silence still emits contract.control in the split-room case.
- No test double in the suite is broken by the Protocol gaining `room`.
notes:
[2026-09-29 03:25:26 UTC] [2026-09-29 POLISH ROUND 3] Use the existing house idiom for the missing
publisher, so this branch reads as the same codebase.

caller_contract/driver.py:495-500, inside the play_audio branch, is the
established shape for "required dependency absent":

    if player is None or getattr(player, "play_asset", None) is None:
        return self._fail(
            FailureReason.TRANSPORT_ERROR,
            "play_audio requires an AudioAssetPlayer (no silent drop)",
            EndedBy.TRANSPORT, completed, spoken,
        )

Mirror it in the dtmf branch when the room gate left the publisher as None:

    if self.dtmf is None:
        return self._fail(
            FailureReason.TRANSPORT_ERROR,
            "dtmf requires a shared sim/agent room; in this SIP leg they are "
            "separate LiveKit rooms and a data packet cannot cross (no silent drop)",
            EndedBy.TRANSPORT, completed, spoken,
        )

The parenthetical is not decoration. "no silent drop" is the codebase's own name
for the principle this entire epic enforces, and reusing it keeps the DTMF
failure legible next to the play_audio failure a reader has already met.
---
[2026-09-29 03:26:27 UTC] [2026-09-29 POLISH ROUND 4] THE GATE RUNS EAGERLY ON EVERY CONTRACT PATH, AND
THE EXISTING TEST FAKES HAVE NO `room`. Read this before writing the
construction site.

THE PROBLEM
`run_contract_driver_path` builds the driver for EVERY contract scenario, not
just ones containing a dtmf step. So whatever you write at the construction site
runs in all 9 test files that exercise this path, including:

  tests/test_contract_live_wiring.py:167   FakeBridge   -- NO `room` attribute
  tests/test_contract_live_wiring.py:231   FakeObserver -- NO `room` attribute
  tests/test_publish_sink_drain.py:45      FakeBridge   -- NO `room` attribute

(the .room grep over FakeObserver's class body returns zero hits.)

Short-circuiting on the bridge side alone is NOT enough. If a FakeBridge ever
gained a truthy `.room`, the very next `observer.room.name` would raise
AttributeError against a FakeObserver that has none -- and it would raise in
every test, not just the new ones.

Write the gate so BOTH sides are guarded and neither raises:

    b_room = getattr(bridge, "room", None)
    o_room = getattr(observer, "room", None)
    _shared = b_room is not None and o_room is not None and b_room.name == o_room.name
    dtmf_pub = (RoomDtmfPublisher(b_room.local_participant)
                if _shared else None)

This returns dtmf_pub=None for every existing fake, which is correct: none of
them has a dtmf step, and a publisher is only ever touched by the dtmf branch.
No existing test needs editing to stay green.

NOTE THE ASYMMETRY WITH THE `local_participant` WARNING
Above, `getattr` is right for the ROOM (it may legitimately be absent on a
stand-in). Inside the shared branch, `getattr(room, "local_participant", None)`
is WRONG, because room.py:224 raises a bare Exception from the property and
getattr does not swallow a raised exception. Access it directly once _shared is
True. The two cases have opposite answers and the distinction is the whole
trap.

title: Ship templates/examples/dtmf-ivr-menu.yaml as the gated user flow
description:
Create templates/examples/dtmf-ivr-menu.yaml. This is the named user flow that
keeps the entire DTMF restore alive under AGENTS.md's no-dead-features rule.

CONTENT

    apiVersion: agent-sim/v1
    kind: Scenario
    metadata:
      id: dtmf-ivr-menu
      locale: en-US
      tags: [dtmf, ivr]
    persona:
      name: Alex
      brief: |
        You are calling a business. An automated assistant reads a keypad
        menu. Press the keys it asks for on your telephone keypad, and answer
        questions with one or two words only.
      style: polite, brief
    execute:
      max_turns: 8
      timeout_s: 120
      first_speaker: user
    caller_steps:
      - do: {behavior: greet, expect: greeting}
      - wait: {seconds: 2}
      - dtmf: "1w2w3w#"
      - wait: {seconds: 3}
      - end: true
    pass_criteria:
      criteria:
      - The agent heard the caller's keypad presses

WHY EACH PIECE
- caller_steps only. Do not use the legacy `script: steps:` surface. That is the
  inert one; the live one is caller_steps.
- The wait AFTER the tones is LOAD-BEARING, not padding. `- dtmf:` followed
  immediately by `- end:` hangs up before the agent can react, so the first
  real run would look broken even though every tone landed.
- Use 'w' in the digit string to exercise the pause path
  ("1w2w3w#"), so the template covers the whole digit parser rather than the
  trivial single-key case.
- Keep it locale en-US. AGENTS.md requires portable defaults; a demo may
  override in its own config, the shipped template may not hardcode one repo's
  language.

DELETE templates/examples/ivr-pin-dtmf.jsonl
It is the example this replaces, and it uses the inert `action: dtmf` legacy
surface which will now be misleading.

DO NOT sweep the other .jsonl files in that directory
There are 17. The amd-* three are pinned by tests/test_amd_templates.py. That
cleanup is a separate commit with its own justification; mixing it in here
makes this diff harder to review and risks breaking a test-pinned template.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- The file parses under the existing template gate.
- test_every_template_has_caller_steps (test_contract_all_templates.py:46-56)
  passes for it, though that test alone is NOT sufficient coverage; the
  spot-drive in the verification sub-epic is the real gate.
- templates/examples/ivr-pin-dtmf.jsonl is gone.
- No other template changed.
notes:
[2026-09-29 03:24:30 UTC] [2026-09-29 POLISH ROUND 2] CORRECTION: the template body in this bead's
description was WRONG in three places. Caught by running the real parser
(`parse_steps`) against it, not by reading it. All three verified empirically
against caller_contract/dsl.py at the current tree.

1. `expect:` IS NOT A `do:` KEY.
     DSLError: unknown do: key(s): ['expect'] (field=do)
   `_parse_do` (dsl.py:328-333) reads only behavior, target, constraints,
   interaction, and rejects anything else. The failure is loud, at parse time,
   which is the good case.

2. `greet` IS NOT IN THE BEHAVIOR CATALOG.
   DEFAULT_BEHAVIOR_CATALOG (dsl.py:37) is exactly:
     accept, arrange_visit, ask, clarify, confirm, deny, end, interrupt,
     negotiate, provide, reject
   `greet` is absent. A scenario may extend the catalog per run via
   parse_steps(..., known_behaviors=...) but the shipped template may not.

3. `wait:` TAKES A BARE INTEGER IN MILLISECONDS, NOT {seconds: N}.
     DSLError: wait: must be a non-negative integer (milliseconds)
   So `- wait: {seconds: 2}` fails. `- wait: 2000` is correct.

CORRECTED caller_steps — VERIFIED to parse, yielding dtmf_digits '1w2w3w#':

    caller_steps:
      - do: {behavior: ask, target: greeting}
      - wait: 2000
      - dtmf: "1w2w3w#"
      - wait: 3000
      - end: true

LESSON FOR EVERY OTHER BEAD IN THIS EPIC
Do not write scenario YAML from memory of the docs. Pipe it through
`parse_steps` / `parse_scenario` and confirm the parsed kinds before committing
it. docs/behavior-dsl.md describes `do:` with an `expect` example that the
parser does not accept, so the doc and the code disagree. Where they disagree,
the parser wins, and only the parser settles it.

title: Fix the authoring warning that promises on the inert legacy surface
description:
authoring.py:308-319 attaches a DTMF promise to the wrong surface:

    dtmf_steps = [s for s in steps if getattr(s, "action", None) == "dtmf"]
    if dtmf_steps and "draft" not in tags:
        findings.append(AuthoringWarning(
            code="dtmf_untagged_draft", severity="info",
            message=("Script action=dtmf present - tag scenario draft until "
                     "the agent under test handles SIP DTMF (sim can send; "
                     "many agents only parse spoken digits).")))

It filters on ScriptStep.action, which is the LEGACY `script: steps:` surface.
That surface has no execution path at all: commit 665ec8c deleted the
ScriptRunner that ran it. The LIVE surface is caller_steps `- dtmf:`, and it
receives no warning whatsoever.

So today the tool warns about a verb that cannot work, and stays silent about
the verb that will.

FIX
Move the filter to CallerAction.kind == "dtmf", or delete the warning. Either
is acceptable. Do not leave a promise attached to a surface that cannot keep it.

If moving it, also check whether the message wording still fits. "Script
action=dtmf" is now inaccurate; the caller-facing syntax is `- dtmf:`.

CONSIDERATION — does the warning still earn its place at all?
Once the restore lands, a dtmf step in a shared-room mode genuinely works, so
the "many agents only parse spoken digits" caveat still has value: agents that
STT the spoken word "one" rather than reading RoomEvent.DtmfReceived will not
react. Keep that substance. What is wrong is only the surface it is attached
to.

DO NOT add a new warning code, a new severity level, or a config knob to control
it. AGENTS.md: no dead surface.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- Either the warning fires for caller_steps dtmf, or it is gone.
- It does not fire for the legacy script action=dtmf surface, which cannot work.
- Existing authoring tests still pass.

title: Update documentation that the DTMF restore makes wrong
description:
Documentation corrections. Every one of these is a statement that becomes FALSE
once the restore lands, so leaving them is a correctness bug, not a nit.

FILES TO CORRECT

docs/contract-caller-wiring.md:61
  Describes dtmf as "planner control only". After the restore it is a real wire
  call with a fail-fast room gate.

docs/guide/installation.md:619
  The ivr-pin-dtmf example is described with `action: dtmf digits`, which is
  the legacy surface. The live syntax is caller_steps `- dtmf: "1"`, and the
  example file itself is being replaced by dtmf-ivr-menu.yaml.

docs/behavior-dsl.md
  Add one line: a keypress appears in events.jsonl as sim.script.dtmf. It is
  NOT a report marker; there is no DTMF chip in the web player.

DO NOT ADD A WEB MARKER
MARKER_DTMF exists at web/report_time.py:21 but is reachable only from a
sim.script.cue spec's interrupt_class (web/markers.py:167,186), and
lks-web/src/lib.rs has zero dtmf hits. Both ports render no chip today. Adding
one means touching web/src types, markers.py, AND the Rust web crate. That is a
separate bead if anyone wants it, not part of this restore.

ONE MORE THING THE DOCSTRING AND DOCS MUST SAY
A sim.script.dtmf event proves the tones were SUBMITTED TO THE LOCAL
PARTICIPANT. It does not prove an agent received them. The server excludes the
sender from data fan-out, so the sim structurally cannot observe its own tone.
Writers reading a run log will otherwise treat the event as delivery proof, and
the archived runs 058/063 (error: null, webrtc_sim mode) are exactly the
misreading that risk invites.

ALSO WORTH ONE LINE
DTMF_CODES is LiveKit's map (# to 11), not RFC 4733 (# to 15). An agent
asserting on SipDTMF.code rather than .digit behaves differently under
simulation than under a real SIP caller.

  dtmf.py module docstring.

title: Verification: unit tests, the tripwire gate, and a real negative check
description:
Sub-epic for proving the restore works and proving it can fail loudly.

Children:
  1. dtmf-tests              tests/test_contract_dtmf.py, 6 cases, offline
  2. dtmf-dsl-test           test_behavior_dsl.py trigger regression guards
  3. dtmf-template-gate-test the tripwire: spot-drive the template, assert the event
  4. dtmf-negative-check     comment out the branch, confirm red, revert

ALL OFFLINE. No conftest, no network. Fakes are per-file, following the
existing convention in tests/test_contract_live_wiring.py.

THE TRIPWIRE IS THE POINT OF THIS SUB-EPIC
Commit 665ec8c deleted working DTMF code and called it dead. It was, by its own
test coverage: the only tests that exercised it were deleted alongside it, so
nothing downstream noticed the capability vanish. This sub-epic is the
structural answer to that.

The existing test_every_template_has_caller_steps
(tests/test_contract_all_templates.py:46-56) only checks caller_actions is
non-empty. It never touches the driver. Delete the dtmf branch and it stays
green. So it is NOT the gate.

dtmf-template-gate-test IS the gate: it drives the shipped template through the
real driver with a fake publisher and asserts a sim.script.dtmf event carrying
the expected digits. Delete the branch and it goes red.

dtmf-negative-check exists to prove that claim rather than assume it. Run it
once, record the outcome, revert. A tripwire that has never been observed to
fire is a hope, not a gate.

BASELINE
dtmf-revert-mutants must have landed and its baseline counts recorded before any
of this is meaningful. Every failure-path assertion here constructs a
ContractDriverFailure or inspects an EndedBy reason; with c0d3e26's mutants
live, all of them land on mutated strings.

title: Write tests/test_contract_dtmf.py covering all six behaviours
description:
New file tests/test_contract_dtmf.py. Drives the real ContractCallerDriver
against a fake participant. Offline.

CASE 1 — digit mapping
RoomDtmfPublisher maps "1w2#" to [(1,"1"), (2,"2"), (11,"#")] and 'w' produces
no tone. Reuses the assertion from the deleted tests/test_script_dtmf_runtime.py
(git show 665ec8c^:tests/test_script_dtmf_runtime.py, lines 129-138) rather
than reinventing it.

CASE 2 — dtmf pushes no PCM
A dtmf step must publish ZERO PCM. This is the original 764dc3a regression and
it is the reason the branch must not route through the publish sink.

This INVERTS an existing test. tests/test_contract_live_wiring.py:685
test_wait_and_dtmf_never_publish currently asserts urlopen was never called for
[{wait:10},{dtmf:"123"},{end:true}] -- it pins the DEFECT. Handle it as:
  - rename it to test_wait_never_publish
  - keep only its `wait` half
  - move the dtmf half here, asserting the opposite
Do not simply delete it; the wait coverage is real.

CASE 3 — a hanging transport fails, it does not hang the run
A fake whose publish_dtmf awaits forever must drive the driver to
FailureReason.TRANSPORT_ERROR within PUBLISH_TIMEOUT_S.

This is the most important case in the file. livekit's Queue overrides
asyncio.Queue.wait_for and drops the timeout (livekit/rtc/_utils.py:103), and
publish_dtmf awaits it with no cancel path (participant.py:320-328). Without
the asyncio.wait_for wrapper in dtmf-module, a dead transport hangs _run_actions
forever; _on_hold_timeout calls bridge.sim_hang_up() without cancelling the
driver task, so the finally: bridge.stop() at run_orchestrator.py:430-431
never runs and the run never finalizes.

Without this test the timeout ships untested and the suite is green while the
wedge ships. Verify the test actually FAILS if you delete the wait_for wrapper.

CASE 4 — a raising transport fails loudly
A publish_dtmf raising PublishDTMFError (livekit/rtc/participant.py:82) fails
the step rather than being swallowed into a generic control event.

CASE 5 — the room gate
With no publisher constructed (the two-room topology), a dtmf step fails with
the message naming that topology, and `silence` still emits contract.control.
This is the bead proving dtmf-room-gate did not silently close.

CASE 6 — trigger gating
`trigger: agent_speaking` on a dtmf step actually waits for the agent before
publishing. Guards the dsl.py change; without it the tone fires at t=0 before
the agent's menu prompt and the historical demo behaviour is lost.

STYLE
Per-file fakes, like tests/test_contract_live_wiring.py. No new conftest.
Async tests use whatever marker the existing async test files use.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- Six cases, all offline, all green.
- Case 3 fails if the wait_for wrapper is removed (prove it, do not assume).
- The renamed wait test retains its wait coverage.
- No test asserts a DTMF chip, a report marker, or a web-rendered element.

title: Add the template tripwire: spot-drive dtmf-ivr-menu through the real driver
description:
This is the single most important test in the restore. It is what makes the
feature non-dead, and it is the thing commit 665ec8c did not have.

WHAT TO ADD
In tests/test_contract_all_templates.py, drive the shipped
templates/examples/dtmf-ivr-menu.yaml through the real ContractCallerDriver
with a fake publisher, and assert that a sim.script.dtmf event is emitted
carrying digits == "1w2w3w#".

WHY THE EXISTING GATE IS NOT ENOUGH
test_every_template_has_caller_steps (:46-56) only asserts
caller_actions is non-empty. It never touches the driver. Comment out the
dtmf branch in driver.py and that test stays GREEN. It is a parse gate, not a
behaviour gate.

Your new test asserts the EVENT, not merely that a publisher was injected.
Asserting injection proves nothing; asserting the event proves the code path
ran.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THIS EPIC
665ec8c deleted 609 lines of working DTMF code plus its 21 tests in one commit
and called it dead. It was dead BY ITS OWN COVERAGE: the only tests that
exercised it were deleted with it, so nothing downstream noticed the capability
disappear from the Python port. This tripwire is the structural answer. If a
future change removes the dtmf branch, this test goes red and names the
template that stopped working.

DEPENDENCIES
Needs dtmf-template landed (the file must exist) and dtmf-driver-branch landed
(the behaviour must exist). This is the last thing to land in the epic.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- The test drives the REAL driver, not a mock of it.
- It asserts a sim.script.dtmf event with the exact expected digit string.
- It fails when the dtmf branch is removed. PROVE this in dtmf-negative-check;
  do not assume it.
- The existing test_every_template_has_caller_steps is untouched and still green.

title: Negative check: comment out the dtmf branch, confirm the tripwire fires, revert
description:
A tripwire that has never been observed to fire is a hope, not a gate. Run this
once, record what happened, revert.

PROCEDURE
  1. Comment out the dtmf branch in caller_contract/driver.py.
  2. Run the suite. Expected: dtmf-template-gate-test goes RED, and
     tests/test_contract_dtmf.py goes red on its dtmf cases.
  3. ALSO confirm the template still PARSES. If it does, that proves
     test_every_template_has_caller_steps is not the keeper and the new spot
     drive is the real gate. This is the specific claim being tested.
  4. Optionally remove the asyncio.wait_for wrapper from dtmf.py and confirm
     dtmf-tests case 3 goes red. That wrapper is the wedge-prevention and it
     has no other coverage.
  5. Revert every edit. `git diff` must be empty afterwards.
  6. Record the observed output on this bead with --notes-push, and on the
     epic.

WHAT A PASS LOOKS LIKE
Both the tripwire AND the timeout test go red, and the template still parses.
If the tripwire stays green, the gate does not exist and dtmf-template-gate-test
must be rewritten before the epic closes.

DO NOT leave the commented-out branch in place. Reverting is part of this
bead's acceptance criteria, not an afterthought.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- Observed red output recorded on this bead and on the epic.
- Template confirmed still parsing with the branch removed.
- git diff is empty at the end; full suite back to the post-restore count.

title: Add dsl regression guards for trigger-on-dtmf
description:
Small addition to tests/test_behavior_dsl.py covering the dsl.py relaxation.

THREE CASES, TWO OF WHICH ARE REGRESSION GUARDS

  1. parse_step({"dtmf": "1", "trigger": {...}}) no longer raises.   [new]
  2. parse_step({"wait": 5, "trigger": {...}}) STILL raises.          [guard]
  3. parse_step({"dtmf": "1", "barge_in": True}) STILL raises.       [guard]

Cases 2 and 3 are the important ones. The dsl change is a two-line deletion
lifting dtmf out of the reject tuple; without guards, a later well-meaning
edit could widen it to wait or to barge_in and nothing would notice. AGENTS.md
calls this out directly: do not let a fix quietly become a feature nobody
asked for.

WHY barge_in STAYS REJECTED FOR dtmf
There is no caller speech to cut across. A keypress has no barge semantics.
Widen it only if someone asks.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- Three cases, green.
- Case 2 and 3 would fail if the dsl change were made too broadly.

title: Rust parity: remove the unwired plan_dtmf twin, align summary

Sub-epic keeping lks and lksr aligned after the restore.

Children:

title: Delete InteractionPlanner.plan_dtmf on BOTH ports atomically
description:
Once dtmf-driver-branch lands, plan_dtmf becomes a second, provably-unwired
representation of a keypress sitting right next to the live one. Delete it.

PYTHON SIDE
  src/livekit_agent_simulator/caller_contract/interaction_planner.py:118
    def plan_dtmf(self, digits: str) -> InteractionOutcome
  Zero src/ callers. The only two callers are:
    tests/test_interaction_planner.py:111  test_plan_dtmf_route
    tests/test_parity_vectors.py:375
  Delete the method, both test callers, and the `dtmf` case in
  tests/fixtures/parity/interaction_planner.json.

RUST SIDE
  src/livekit_agent_simulator_rust/crates/lks-core/src/caller_contract.rs:1678
    pub fn plan_dtmf(digits: &str) -> InteractionOutcome
  Its sole caller is at :2561, inside #[cfg(test)] mod parity_tests.
  Note Rust enumerates top-level parity fixtures from a hardcoded
  VALIDATOR_VECTOR_FILES list at caller_contract.rs:2153 -- if you add or
  remove a top-level fixture file, that list moves too. Removing a `dtmf`
  case from an existing file does not.

THIS MUST BE ONE ATOMIC CHANGE. DO NOT SPLIT BY LANGUAGE
tests/test_parity_vectors.py and the Rust parity_tests share
tests/fixtures/parity/interaction_planner.json. Deleting the Python half alone
leaves a Rust test calling a method that no longer has a Python twin; deleting
the Rust half alone leaves the same hole the other way. The fixture is shared
state, so both sides move together or neither does. This is one commit with
one message, even though it touches two toolchains.

WHAT plan_dtmf WAS AND WHY IT IS NOT THE RIGHT SEAM
It classifies an InteractionOutcome with kind=InteractionActionKind.Dtmf and
carries dtmf_digits. It has no timing, no pacing, no trigger, and no test
beyond asserting that classification. It was never a delivery path and must not
become one.

DO NOT route the new driver branch through the planner to "reuse" it. That
would drag a classification-only abstraction into the delivery path and give it
responsibilities it has no tests for. The driver calls DtmfPublisher directly.

WHY NOT LEAVE IT
AGENTS.md: "Dev-stage cleanliness -- no legacy paths. Delete dead config,
unused fields, and half-features in the same change." A dead keypress
representation sitting next to a live one is exactly the half-feature that rule
targets. And the whole reason 665ec8c's deletion went unnoticed is that dead
DTMF code accumulated quietly.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- plan_dtmf gone from both ports; parity fixtures consistent.
- uv run --extra dev pytest -q green.
- cargo test --workspace green.
- No new indirection between the driver and DtmfPublisher.

title: Align lks-core summary.rs to the four-kind script_action_kinds set

port emitted sim.script.dtmf from the contract path, so the divergence was

title: Follow-on: real DTMF for the two-room SIP legs
description:
FOLLOW-ON EPIC. Not part of the restore. The restore makes this gap LOUD; it
does not close it. File this so the fail-fast is not mistaken for delivery.

THE GAP
publish_dtmf is a room broadcast. In inbound_sip, outbound_sim_callee and
agent_dials the sim sits in lks-sip-{run_id} while the agent is in a different
room. Correct delivery needs a participant in the AGENT room that the agent
perceives as the caller.

Real DTMF is a PSTN use case, and PSTN is exactly this topology.

WHY THE OBVIOUS FIXES DO NOT WORK
Publishing from the observer's room reaches the right room but the wrong
sender: the observer connects as lks-obs-{run_id[:8]} and voice-ai-agent drops
any sender that is not its first remote participant
(voice-ai-agent/src/session/attach-flow-runtime.ts:729). Right room, wrong
sender. That is why the restore gates rather than picking one.

OPTIONS, in rough order of correctness
  (a) A dedicated caller-identity participant in the agent room, coordinated by
      SimLegHandle. Correct and the most invasive.
  (b) Relax the consumer filter to accept any sender. Cheapest; moves the
      correctness burden onto voice-ai-agent and weakens their agent.
  (c) Accept the limitation. Legitimate if no current consumer flow needs it.

CURRENT STATE OF DEMAND
Two agents in the consumer's DB have a DTMF_INPUT node. Both were authored
against the shared-room paths. No verified flow requires PSTN DTMF today, which
is why the restore ships with a gate rather than this plumbing.

BEFORE STARTING
Re-run the consumer DB query (see the epic description for the SQL). If a flow
now targets a SIP leg, this stops being P3 and gets promoted.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (for whenever it is picked up)
- A dtmf step delivers to the agent in a real two-room SIP leg, evidenced by
  the agent's own reaction, not by the absence of an error in events.jsonl.

title: Live smoke: press keys against a real DTMF_INPUT agent and record its reaction
description:
Everything else in this verification sub-epic is offline. This bead is the one
that proves the tones actually reach an agent. It is the ONLY acceptable
delivery evidence, for a structural reason.

WHY AN OFFLINE TEST CANNOT PROVE DELIVERY
publish_dtmf is a room broadcast and the server EXCLUDES THE SENDER from data
fan-out. The sim therefore structurally CANNOT observe its own tone. A green
offline suite proves the code path ran and the SDK call returned; it cannot
prove an agent received the digit. The archived runs 058/063 show error: null,
which is exactly this limitation being misread as proof.

The only real evidence is the agent's own reaction.

TARGET AGENT
Use the consumer flow verified in the epic description:

  postgresql://dev_user@localhost:5432/voice_ai_local
  SELECT f."agentId", a.name FROM "FlowNode" n
  JOIN "AgentFlow" f ON f.id = n."flowId" JOIN "Agent" a ON a.id = f."agentId"
  WHERE n.type = 'DTMF_INPUT';
    agent_g9srhevzdanmpue372yfgzi7   イーブロード
    agent_w3ph2c35kisb1ibqythi571j   イーブロード (3-Cụm Macro-Node)

agent_w3ph2c35kisb1ibqythi571j is the better target. Its DTMF_INPUT node
(xr617az7554nbwvkndfe86ro) is single_key with acceptedKeys 1/2/3 and four
DTMF-triggered transitions routing on {{dtmf_value}} == "1" | "2" | "3" plus a
dtmf_timeout handle. All three keys route to the SAME downstream node, so a
transcript diff will not distinguish them; use the transition's own effects or
the timeout path as the discriminator.

This flow is shared-room capable, so it exercises the working path. It does NOT
exercise the two-room gap; see the PSTN follow-on bead.

WHAT TO RECORD, WITH DETAILED LOGGING
This bead exists partly because run logs are the deliverable. Capture, per press:
  - the sim.script.dtmf event: digits, published count, error
  - the agent's transcript immediately after, quoted
  - the agent's transition actually taken (Cụm 1 vs Cụm 0 - Timeout)
  - the wall-clock gap between the tone and the agent's first word
  - the final events.jsonl retained under the target repo's .agent-sim/reports/

ASSERTION
A press of "1" reaches Cụm 1 - Thu thập thông tin. Silence or a timeout
transition instead is a FAIL even if sim.script.dtmf reported published: 1.
That divergence is the exact failure the restore must not ship.

ALSO RUN THE SHIPPED TEMPLATE
lks execute dtmf-ivr-menu --root <path> against the agent, so the shipped
template has a real run behind it and not just a spot-drive.

ENVIRONMENT CAVEATS
This is the one bead that needs real credentials and a running LiveKit
project, so it may be deferred in CI. It is NOT optional for closing the epic;
if it cannot run, say so explicitly rather than letting the epic close on
offline tests alone.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- A real run exists with a retained events.jsonl.
- The agent's transcript shows a reaction to the pressed digit.
- The timeout transition was NOT taken on a successful press.
- Any failure is recorded honestly, not retried into a pass.

title: Decide the fate of the inert legacy script: action=dtmf parse surface
description:
DECISION + EXECUTION BEAD. Not resolved by the plan; surfaced by review.

THE PROBLEM IS A DUAL PATH
After the restore there are two ways to author a keypress in the Python port:

  A. caller_steps: - dtmf: "1"     LIVE. Executes, emits sim.script.dtmf.
  B. script: steps: - action: dtmf  INERT. Parses, never executes.

B still parses cleanly. script/models.py:9 lists "dtmf" in SUPPORTED_ACTIONS,
script_parse accepts it, and nothing runs it, because 665ec8c deleted the
ScriptRunner that did. So B is a verb that parses, runs, and does nothing --
the exact shape of the defect this epic fixes, just one layer down.

AGENTS.md is unambiguous on this: "No legacy shims / dual config names -- clean
breaks are fine while pre-1.0." And: "Delete dead config, unused fields, and
half-features in the same change."

WHY A RESEARCH PANEL PROPOSED DELETING IT AND LOST
Design 3 proposed deleting surface B outright. It was rejected because Rust's
contract path PROJECTS caller steps onto the script surface
(lks-core/src/scenario.rs:805-808 to :446-454 to ScriptRuntime). Deleting B in
Python while Rust still routes through it widens the divergence it claimed to
close.

That reasoning was sound for making B the ONE surface. It does not settle what
to do with B itself. Neither does it apply to Rust, where B is live.

OPTIONS
(a) Leave B parsing. Cost: a dual path that silently no-ops. Mitigation: the
    authoring-warning bead moves the warning onto caller_steps, which makes B
    quietly rather than loudly wrong.
(b) Delete B from Python, keep it in Rust. Clean break, honest to the actual
    runtime, but the ports then accept different scenarios.
(c) Make B hard-error in Python with a migration message pointing at
    `- dtmf:`. Loud, actionable, and preserves parse compatibility with Rust
    while refusing to no-op.

RECOMMENDATION: (c). It is the only option that neither lies to the author nor
splits the ports' accepted grammar. A hard error with a one-line migration
hint is a clean break in effect while staying compatible on paper, which is
what pre-1.0 wants.

BEFORE DECIDING
Check what would actually break. `grep -rn "action: dtmf\|action.*dtmf" templates/
demo/ docs/` -- and remember templates/examples/ivr-pin-dtmf.jsonl is being
deleted by the template bead regardless. If nothing outside docs ships it,
(c) is cheap.

DO NOT delete B in the Rust port. It is live there.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- Decision recorded with reasoning on this bead and on the epic.
- Whatever is chosen is implemented and tested.
- No surface parses a keypress without either executing it or erroring loudly.

WHAT THEY ACTUALLY DO — verified, not inferred

notes:
SCOPE UPDATE 2026-09-30 (after the queue + gate + post-run fixes).

DEFECT 1 — THE CATALOG IS NOT A CONTROL SURFACE — RESOLVED, and it was never a contract problem.

Measured offline against the peer session's own catalog and the live router endpoint: turn 5 of run 013 ("provide your callback phone number") routes to `callback_number` correctly, in 3.0s. Prompt, catalog and schema were never wrong.

The observed decisions were always the CORRECT answer for the NEXT question. The real cause was upstream: `observer.last_agent_final_text` is a single overwrite slot, and `wait_agent_turn` only returns a final once `agent_is_active_speaker` is false — a VAD flag that lags real audio by ~2.4s. Turn N's final was overwritten by turn N+1's before the flag cleared. FIXED (e7f68f0): finals are queued on arrival and drained oldest-first.

The `probabilities` / logprobs remedy is DROPPED. It would have added an abstain rule to a router that already picks correctly, turning a correct turn into `off_script`.

Run 027 (happy path, no barge) was ALWAYS correct — one decision per agent final, in order. Both runs are now pinned against their artifacts in tests/test_turn_alignment_order.py, because they disagree and an earlier acceptance criterion proposed "fixing" 027 by flipping its turn 2, which would have broken a correct run.

RESIDUAL, recorded not hidden: tier 2 (session snapshot) and tier 3 (the "[untranscribed agent speech]" audio floor) are separate evidence sources that bypass the queue and can still be one turn behind. That is the likely cause of run 013 turn 3 routing an untranscribed turn to a real entry.

DEFECT 2 — THE JUDGE ERRORED ON EVERY RUN — narrowed, not yet fixed.

Measured on the peer session's live endpoint: the transcript path is fine (4 rows, real text), the prompt is 4573 chars, a real judge call returns 200 with a well-formed verdict in 26.25s against a 180s timeout, and judge_run_multi is ONE call. So the timeout is explained by none of: endpoint, config, prompt size, call count. Not reproducible from the artifacts available. The failure is now diagnosable: evals/runner.py reports prompt_chars, transcript_chars, criteria, turns and elapsed_s, so the next occurrence is readable in one pass (4f6840c).

While investigating, two adjacent false-pass bugs were found and fixed:
  - af924f8: `ok = not hard_fail` meant an UNGRADED run reported the same `ok` as a passing one. Now three distinct states: pass / hard / ungraded.
  - f3aef28: a fault in post-run bookkeeping (sqlite, after_run hooks) escaped and returned `run_id: null`, orphaning a paid run's transcript on disk with nothing pointing at it (run 033).

CLOSE WHEN
  1. a barge-in run routes each agent line to the response that answers IT, verified on a fresh run's events.jsonl — not inferred from the router in isolation.
  2. the judge returns a real verdict on a run that is graded.

Suite at last measurement: 1434 Python passed, 0 failed; 29 Rust lks-core binaries and 39 lks-livekit tests green.

title: Research: provider enum guarantees and the v1 schema shape
description:
RESEARCH — NO CODE IN src/. Gates .3, .6, .7. Source: docs/plans/response-router.md §7 "Still open".

The enum handed to the provider is generated at RUNTIME from the scenario's response ids, so the v1
schema shape depends on what each provider actually accepts. Getting this wrong fails at call time,
on a run, instead of at parse time.

ANSWER WITH PRIMARY SOURCES (vendor docs, not blog posts)
1. OpenAI Structured Outputs strict mode: must every property be in `required`? Is
   additionalProperties:false mandatory? Enum-size or schema-byte limits, and what happens when
   exceeded? Does a BARE top-level {"enum":[...]} work or must it be wrapped as
   {"responseId": "..."}? When the model declines for safety, what does the API return — a
   distinct refusal status, or a schema-shaped body? The contract requires a valid responseId
   ALWAYS, so the refusal path must be identified and mapped explicitly.
2. Gemini structured output (responseMimeType + responseSchema): strict subset or advisory?
   ENFORCE or encourage? enum support? bare vs wrapped? nesting and size limits? What exactly
   comes back for candidates==[], empty parts, and {} (emitted when `required` is omitted, because
   all Gemini properties are optional by default)?
   The plugin records that gemini-2.0-flash 404s on the working key — confirm the working alias.
3. VERDICT for v1: which provider's guarantee is STRONGER at preventing an out-of-set label, and
   does either ever return a value outside the enum? Pick ONE shape for both adapters. Default to
   the wrapped form unless a bare enum is provably accepted by both.
4. Record the MAX_RESPONSES ceiling as a number with its source, so .3 turns it into a PARSE-TIME
   error rather than a call-time 400 blamed on the agent.

AGENTS.md rule: if docs and the installed package in .venv disagree, TRUST .venv and say so in the
note.

DELIVERABLE
Replace the open question in docs/plans/response-router.md §7 with: chosen schema shape, enum
ceiling + citation, refusal contract per provider, degenerate-case behaviour per provider.
close_reason:
Research complete and folded into docs/plans/response-router.md (new 'Schema shape and limits' section) and responses.py.

Resolved: the enum MUST be wrapped (a bare top-level enum is invalid on OpenAI); two published ceilings - 1000 enum values, and 15000 total enum-string chars above 250 values, the second usually binding first; refusal arrives as HTTP 200 with content[].type=='refusal', not a distinct status; Gemini publishes no numeric enum cap, so the OpenAI ceilings are the conservative shared bound.

The length rule found a real defect in code written before the research landed: responses.py originally checked catalog COUNT only, which would have waved a 400-id catalog through to a live 400. Both rules are now enforced at parse with file:line. Adversarial verify returned refuted=false; the open items it raised are citation and pricing nits, not load-bearing claims.

## POLISH ROUND 8 (2026-09-29) — under-specification found

### UNDER-SPECIFICATION — the routed context has an unset key, and a trap in filling it

Rounds 1-7 checked what EXISTS. Round 8 read the beads as an implementer would and found a place
where they would have to guess — and where guessing wrong would defeat the feature.

VERIFIED
  - `relevant_facts` is a `run()` keyword (driver.py:209), copied into `facts` at driver.py:241,
    and passed into the context as `relevant_facts` (language_adapter.py:86).
  - NOTHING supplies it. grep for `relevant_facts` outside driver.py and language_adapter.py
    returns nothing — `live_wiring.py` does not pass it. In every real run today it is `None`
    -> `[]`.
  - AGENTS.md describes it as "Context.caller_knows / world — optional facts the persona already
    knows (injected)". It is a persona-background channel, and it is currently dead weight.

THE TRAP
The routed context must carry the line to speak. Round 7's bead text says build_routed_context
returns "the SAME key shape plus one added key, canonical_text". An implementer reaching for the
"same shape" will face an empty `relevant_facts` and have to decide what to do with it. The two
available answers are both wrong in different ways:

  WRONG: put the catalog entry's `text` into `relevant_facts` as well as `canonical_text`.
     The model then sees the answer framed as a KNOWN FACT and as the line to phrase, and will
     paraphrase around it or embellish it. The router's entire purpose is that the caller says the
     AUTHORED thing.
  ALSO WRONG: leave the key present but empty and hope the prompt ignores it. That is a standing
     invitation for a later contributor to "fix" it by populating it, and the resulting regression
    would look like a random prompt-quality drift.

DECIDE EXPLICITLY IN THIS BEAD
1. `relevant_facts` is NOT the place for the catalog text. `canonical_text` is, and only that.
2. On the routed path either (a) omit `relevant_facts` from the context entirely, or (b) keep the
   key with the persona's real facts, which today is `[]`. Choose one and say which. (a) is leaner
   and removes a dead channel; (b) preserves one prompt shape across both paths. Either is
   defensible — leaving it undecided is not.
3. State the REJECTED option and the reason, so the next contributor does not "restore" it.
4. Confirm the text backend will not invent detail absent from `canonical_text`. The existing
   _SYSTEM_PROMPT already constrains on-topic phrasing; decide whether the routed context needs an
   additional clause of the form "say `canonical_text`; add nothing that is not in it", and if so
   put it in the prompt bead's snapshot test (which will then fail if the clause is dropped).

TESTS
- the routed context contains canonical_text and does NOT contain the catalog text under
  `relevant_facts`
- with `relevant_facts` empty (today's real state), the rendered text-backend prompt is byte-stable
  and the output paraphrase does not introduce facts absent from canonical_text

title: Turn alignment: gate the silence trigger on a real turn-completion signal
description:
SEPARATE DEFECT, OWN PARENT. This is PROBLEMS.md §1. The response router does NOT fix it, and a
caller can lose a turn with or without a router — the router will not even know.

MEASURED ON LIVE RUNS
`silence` triggers gate on AgentTurnWait.is_agent_speaking_now() -> Observer.agent_is_active_speaker,
set ONLY from LiveKit's active_speakers_changed event (livekit/observer.py:242-250). That signal LAGS
the agent's real audio by ~2.4s, so the trigger can satisfy "agent has been silent for delay_ms"
while the agent is mid-turn:

    15406 ms  agent transcript final lands          (agent is audibly speaking)
    17360 ms  contract.trigger_fired kind=silence  <- fired anyway
    17781 ms  active_speakers: [agent]               <- flag only turns up now
    18296 ms  active_speakers: [agent]
    19093 ms  active_speakers: [agent, lks-caller]
    20390 ms  contract.say_published (caller)       <- lands inside the agent's window

The caller then spoke during agent speech and the utterance was NEVER delivered to the agent as a
user turn: extracted_company_name stayed null for the rest of the call and the flow re-asked 3-4
times. The identical scripted line at delay_ms 6500 was captured perfectly (run 036).

TWO DISTINCT CAUSES, DO NOT CONFLATE
- The harness fires the trigger too early (active_speakers lag). FIXABLE HERE.
- The agent then dropped the overlapping utterance. That is the agent platform, not the harness —
  voice-ai-agent docs/plans/gpt-live-queue-race-design.md §A.8/A.9: DuplexRealtimeSession.interrupt()
  is an empty body, the adapter declares messageTruncation: false, and "you can't stop the model,
  but you can stop playing its audio to the user". Fixing the trigger removes the overlap, which is
  the only lever the harness has.
close_reason: Parent. Research (.1) delivered d3d4b79: the signal is the participant attribute lk.agent.state, NOT an event - agent_state_changed exists only in the agent-worker protocol, absent from the client SDK's EventTypes, and Observer.attach registers no participant_attributes_changed handler. Implementation (.2) landed: attribute tracked in observer.py and preferred in ObserverAgentWait.is_agent_speaking_now, with the energy fallback preserved but RECORDED via contract.agent_state_unavailable. The falsifiable claim is still open by design: whether listening lands after the last audio frame needs a live duplex run, and the symmetric barge-in-at-the-tail failure is exactly as bad as the one being fixed.

title: Research: a trustworthy agent-turn-completion signal
description:
RESEARCH — gates turn-alignment.2.

ANSWER
1. Does the simulator already subscribe to agent_state_changed (AgentStateChanged: initializing |
   idle | listening | thinking | speaking) or user_state_changed? Name the EXACT observer field. A
   caller gated on speaking -> not-speaking is gated on the agent's own state machine, not on audio
   energy.
2. Is that signal available and timely for a DUPLEX transport, or only for turn-based? The transcript
   is the EARLIER signal (15.4s vs 17.8s) so it is NOT a substitute — the question is whether agent
   state is a better third option. Measure the lag of each candidate against the same run.
3. What does LiveKit document about waiting for a genuine turn end?
   https://docs.livekit.io/agents/logic/turns/

DO NOT "FIX" THIS BY RAISING THE DELAY
A longer delay is symptom-masking and not free: the model self-prompts during caller silence, so a
longer window means more off-script filler. AGENTS.md "no stubborn patches — defaults first", and its
smell test: "if the patch only makes sense for one scenario id or one failure screenshot, it is
probably wrong". Fix the wrong SIGNAL, not the number.

DELIVERABLE
Update PROBLEMS.md §1 with: the chosen signal, the observer field that carries it, measured lag, and
what has to be wired.
close_reason: Researched and written up in PROBLEMS.md section 1, commit d3d4b79. Docs-only, no code change, no delay numbers touched per the bead's own instruction. ANSWERS: (1) No, the simulator does not subscribe to agent_state_changed, and it CANNOT - that event exists only in the agent-worker IPC protocol (livekit.protocol.agent_pb.agent_session). The client SDK declares 35 events in EventTypes (livekit/rtc/room.py:54) and agent_state_changed is not among them; grep agent_state over livekit/rtc/*.py returns nothing. Observer.attach() at livekit/observer.py:202 registers exactly 6 handlers and participant_attributes_changed is not one. (2) The state does reach a client by another road: the agent writes the participant attribute lk.agent.state, values exactly 'idle'|'initializing'|'listening'|'thinking'|'speaking'. Verified end to end - agents-js setAttributes in livekit/agents/voice/room_io/room_io.ts, ATTRIBUTE_AGENT_STATE in livekit/agents/types.py, the JSON Schema behind client-sdk-js attribute-typings.ts, and the client dispatch at livekit/rtc/room.py:924-936 emitting (changed_attributes dict, participant) so the handler is a dict lookup, not a diff walk. (3) LiveKit documents the attribute for frontend reaction and recommends state getters over raw state; the turns docs cover USER-side turn detection, not agent-side turn completion, which is the half we need. title: Give the router an abort path an operator can use mid-incident
description:
FOUND IN POLISH ROUND 4. VERIFIED ABSENT: grep over src/ for no_router | disable_router |
router_enabled returns nothing.

THE HAZARD
This feature changes what the simulated caller SAYS. If a router change ships misrouting in a
target repo, the current answer is "edit the scenario file to remove the responses block" — which
means editing a file inside someone else's repo, mid-incident, to stop a bad test run. That is not an
abort path.

WHY text_planner.enabled:false IS NOT ONE
It only switches the WORDING layer. The router still selects responseIds, still records verdicts,
and still bypasses the validator. A run that is misrouting stays misrouting.

REQUIREMENT
Exactly ONE documented, tested way to force a router-enabled scenario to run the caller_steps path
for a single run, without editing the scenario. Choose the mechanism deliberately and record the
choice in this bead's close reason:
  (a) a run-time CLI override (e.g. `lks execute <id> --no-router`), or
  (b) a config key, or
  (c) an environment variable.
AGENTS.md preference order: a runtime override beats a persistent config key, because a config key
left set to false in a target repo is itself a second source of truth — and an incident-time flag
that stays off is a security-shaped footgun. A CLI flag is the likely answer; justify whatever you
pick.

RULES
- It must be a genuine bypass, not a warning: caller_steps wins, no router call, no verdicts, no
  contract.router_* events.
- It must be REFUSED as a no-op on a scenario that has no responses catalog, rather than silently
  accepted — otherwise it becomes a knob nobody can trust.
- Do NOT add a permanent `router.enabled` key. If (b) is chosen, say why in the close reason and
  make it obvious that it is incident tooling, not a mode.

TESTS
- a router scenario run with the abort falls back to caller_steps and emits zero router events
- a caller_steps scenario run with the abort is REFUSED, not silently accepted
- the abort is visible in the run summary, so a report cannot be mistaken for a routed run
- the flag appears in `lks execute --help` and in the MCP tool description (see the CLI+MCP bead)
notes:
NOT DONE. Reverted; src/ is at HEAD, suite 1293 passed / 0 failed.

WHAT IS ESTABLISHED (design settled, only the plumbing is missing)
- Mechanism CHOSEN: a run-time CLI override, lks execute <id> --no-router. Not a config key - a key
  left set to false is itself a second source of truth, and a flag in a shell history is not.
  Record this choice in the close reason when it lands.
- It must bypass the ROUTER, not the wording layer. text_planner.enabled:false is not equivalent:
  the router would still pick responseIds, still record verdicts, and still bypass the validator, so
  a misrouting run stays misrouting.
- The abort must be RECORDED, not silent - emit contract.router_aborted with the reason and the
  skipped response ids. A run that did not exercise the router must never be mistaken for one that
  did and passed.

WHY THIS ATTEMPT FAILED - THE TRAP, SO THE NEXT ONE DOES NOT REPEAT IT
Threading one flag through cli.py -> ops.execute_scenario -> run_scenario -> run_scenario_instance
means touching FOUR signatures, and patching them with a regex misfires: it placed no_router on
run_scenario instead of run_scenario_instance, and on a second pass produced
'parameter without a default follows parameter with a default'. Two syntax errors, both from the
same shortcut, both caught only by diffing the copy first - which is why the diff-verify step is
not optional.

DO IT THIS WAY
Edit each signature BY HAND with the Edit tool, one call per signature, reading the real text
first. The four sites are: cli.execute (option + forward), ops.execute_scenario (param + forward),
run_scenario (param + forward), run_scenario_instance (param + the emit). A regex over
'def name(...)' cannot tell these four apart - they share a prefix.

Then: does the bypass actually skip the branch? The driver gates on
'router is not None and response_catalog is not None', so the abort has to CLEAR one of those on
the scenario/driver for the run, not merely skip an emit. Decide where that lives - setting
scenario.responses = None before the run is the simplest and is what the emit should record.
close_reason: commit bda3cb6. --no-router is a run-time flag threaded cli.execute -> ops.execute_scenario -> run_scenario -> run_scenario_instance. It clears scenario.responses before the contract path, so the driver's response_catalog gate is false; clearing is load-bearing, skipping the emit is not. contract.router_aborted records that the router was not exercised. text_planner.enabled:false is NOT equivalent - the router would still route, still record verdicts, still bypass the validator. Suite 1302 passed / 2 skipped / 2 xfailed / 0 failed.

## WIRING NOTE (2026-09-29) — one edge deliberately NOT added

The Rust-parity synthesis proposed an edge `v2-4-i4g -> this bead`, labelled "informational" because
its option (a) depends on the router config block from i4g existing.

It was attempted and `br dep add` REJECTED IT: it closes a real cycle.

    i4g -> ini -> bx2 -> i4g

`bx2 -> i4g` was already wired when bx2 was created, and `ini -> bx2` is the hard edge that prevents
the lks-init P0 from shipping. Adding `i4g -> ini` would make i4g depend on ini, which depends on
bx2, which depends on i4g.

The cycle checker is right and the edge is not informational — it is impossible. The dependency it
was expressing (ini needs i4g first) is already satisfied transitively: `ini -> bx2 -> i4g` means
ini cannot run before bx2, and bx2 cannot run before i4g. The order this bead needs is enforced
without the extra edge.

Recorded here so nobody re-attempts it and assumes a different outcome.

RESOLUTION: the catalog is shown COMMENTED OUT in every scenario template, matching the pattern templates/config.yaml already used. A commented block is invisible to the parser, so the scaffolded scenario runs as plain caller_steps while the shape is documented in place; both beads' actual goals hold.
