title: DECISION: what does lksr do when a scenario carries responses: and a router is configured
description:
DECISION BEAD. Record the answer with `br update --notes-push`, then close. Mirrors the shape of
livekit-agent-simulator-dtmf-restore-python-3tv.3.

THE QUESTION
Does lksr ever learn to execute a routed run, or does the Rust port stay at the v1 surface?
This bead RECORDS the answer. It implements nothing; v2-29-agt is the only Rust code this migration
ships.

THE PREMISE CORRECTION THAT CHANGES THE EXPOSURE CALCULATION
The migration does NOT delete caller_steps. D13 (response-router.md:140, :537-539) keeps it
mandatory: "`caller_steps` remains mandatory (run_orchestrator.py:406-411,
tests/test_contract_all_templates.py:45-53), so no skeleton synthesis". Plan §10 Q2 keeps
responses-only an open owner question. v2-8-0f6 POLISH ROUND 4: "when BOTH are present,
caller_steps WINS and the router is not engaged." So no lksr user is stranded on a removed path.

WHAT §7 GETS RIGHT AND WHAT IT GETS WRONG
Right: KNOWN_KINDS is `[&str; 13]` (scenario.rs:19-33) containing "CallerSteps" and no "Responses",
and scenario_jsonl.rs:185 hard-rejects unknown kinds.
Wrong in three ways:
  (a) "the exclusion is stated in the plan and in AGENTS.md" is FALSE. AGENTS.md is 258 lines with
      ZERO occurrences of lksr, router, python-only, or divergence — the only "rust" strings are
      "trust .venv" (:104) and beads_rust (:204, the issue tracker). README.md is equally silent.
  (b) "tests/golden/ is empty, so nothing catches it today" is STALE. crates/lks-core/tests/golden/
      holds 4 files dated 2026-09-03. The conclusion survives; the stated reason does not.
  (c) It justifies itself by the ABSENCE of a gate. That is the exact reasoning 3tv.6 was created
      to structurally answer: "Commit 665ec8c deleted working DTMF code and called it dead. It was,
      by its own test coverage: the only tests that exercised it were deleted alongside it."

THE INPUTS
  FOR OUT OF SCOPE
  - Two independent release trains: python-release.yml:5-7 `v*` minus `v*-rust*`; rust-release.yml:5-6
    `v*-rust*`. A Python cut breaks no Rust artifact.
  - No Windows artifact exists (rust-release.yml:27-33, webrtc-sys abseil; install.ps1:118-122
    hard-throws). Exposure on the largest platform is structurally zero.
  - Python is the default (install.sh:24 `RUST=0`); lksr is opt-in behind `--rust`/`-Rust`.

title: Rust fail-fast: lksr names an unimplemented router, on the same predicate Python uses
description:
Implements the fail-fast arm of v2-28-rst. This is the ENTIRE Rust code delta for this migration.
It is NOT a router port and NOT a parity slice of one. It is a guard, on the correct predicate,
at the only call site that can evaluate it.

THE PREDICATE — get this right or the bead is actively harmful.
The plan's own predicate is `uses_router()` = responses: present AND a configured router
(response-router.md:945, :1130-1136). Do NOT guard on "contains responses:" alone. Plan :1143 is
explicit: "a parsed-but-unused `responses:` block changes nothing", and :949 "every run behaves
identically". A `responses:` block with no router configured is INERT AND CORRECT — both ports
agree — and failing fast there would break `lksr` on every stock template for no benefit.

DO NOT put the guard in the parse layer. scenario_from_dict (scenario.rs:653) cannot see config, so
`uses_router()` is structurally unreachable from that call site. Putting it there also breaks
byte-parity: scenario.rs:1 declares itself "byte-parity port of scenario.py + scenario_from_dict.py",
and f8k invariant 1 says "Python parity is the contract".

NEVER ship the blanket "no unconsumed top-level keys" guard. I enumerated the keys
scenario_from_dict actually consumes: metadata, id, simulator, execute, run, dispatch, caller,
telephony, script, persona, plugins, plugin_modules, assert, asserts, behavior, caller_steps,
pass_criteria, pass_criteria_mode, pass_judges, locale, tags, context. It does NOT consume
`apiVersion` or `kind` — yet 22 of 23 shipped .yaml templates carry both, and Rust's own writer EMITS
both (scenario_yaml.rs:140-141). That guard makes lksr unable to load any scenario in the package
and reds out export_parity.rs:7-20 and golden_scenario.rs:91,159, which write those keys then
re-parse with .expect().

SITE 1 — the guard, at the run wiring, not the parse.
  src/livekit_agent_simulator_rust/crates/lks-livekit/src/run.rs, at BOTH contract-path gates
  (:721 and :754, `.with_contract_only(!scenario.caller_actions.is_empty())`). Both are inside the
  function that already has the config in hand. Add, adjacent to each:

      if !scenario.responses.is_empty() && cfg.router.is_some() {
          return Err(... "this scenario is configured for the v2 responses router, which lksr does
          not implement; run it with Python `lks`, or unset the `router:` block in
          .agent-sim/config.yaml ..." );
      }

  This is SYMMETRIC with Python's ConfigError at plan :1119-1122 — same condition, both ports.
  The error must name BOTH remedies, because for a user with no router configured, "use Python" is
  wrong advice: their run is correct as-is.

SITE 2 — read the field so the guard has something to read.
  scenario.rs: add `responses` to the Scenario struct and to scenario_from_dict, next to the
  caller_steps arm at :787. Add "Responses" to KNOWN_KINDS (:19-33, bump [13] -> [14]) so the JSONL
  path stops hard-rejecting and routes through the SAME struct and the SAME guard. Two formats
  behaving differently on the same input is the asymmetry the guard exists to remove.
  Reject per-key on VALUE shape only where Python also rejects (see v2-3-w06's error paths) — do
  not build a full catalog parser here. That is v2-27-aut's dead end and AGENTS.md:68 forbids it.

SITE 3 — export, so parse-without-export cannot recur.
  scenario_yaml.rs: add the export arm beside the caller_steps export, so a responses: block
  survives `lksr export` / `lksr convert` / MCP `export_scenario`. This is caller_dsl.rs:9's own
  stated contract — "preserve fields on export" — and it prevents the exact mirror of plan :539's
  warning ("Parse-without-export silently drops the catalog").

WHAT THIS BEAD DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO
  - No responses loop in lks-livekit/src/script.rs. No router, no planner, no provider adapter.
  - No catalog semantics: no id uniqueness, no reserved-id rules, no system-entry rules. Those
    belong with the Python parser (v2-3-w06) and are not needed to make the guard correct.
  - No `router` key in Rust's SimConfig / config_snapshot. config.rs has no router knowledge and
    load_config does not reject unknown top-level keys, so a `router:` block is silently dropped
    from Rust's config_snapshot. That divergence becomes visible ONLY once a router is configured
    in the user's config — which is exactly when this guard fires and tells them to use Python.
    Say so in the bead so the next migration does not rediscover it.
  - DO NOT touch the caller_steps path. D13 keeps it mandatory; "CallerSteps" stays in KNOWN_KINDS;
    scenario.rs:395-517 keeps projecting all 9 step kinds.

TESTS — the two that matter are the negatives
  - A YAML scenario with `responses:` AND a configured router: run.rs returns the named error.
  - NEGATIVE CONTROL 1: a YAML scenario with `responses:` and NO configured router: runs normally.
    Without this test, the guard regresses the stock-template path and goes green.
  - NEGATIVE CONTROL 2: a STOCK v1 template (any of the 22 carrying apiVersion/kind) still loads
    through load_scenario_yaml unchanged. This is the assertion that catches the blanket-guard
    variant, and it is absent from every earlier draft of this work.
  - JSONL: a `Responses` record no longer hard-rejects at scenario_jsonl.rs:185; it parses and hits
    the same run-wiring guard.
  - export round-trip: a responses: block survives `lksr export` byte-identically.
  - `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p lks-core` all green —
    requires v2-26-fmt first.

BLOCKS nothing in Python. Blocks nothing in Rust.
close_reason: commit c426439. The refusal is SYMMETRIC with Python's ConfigError, which is what makes it trustworthy: both ports decide from the same predicate or the same scenario behaves differently under lks and lksr with nothing saying why. PREDICATE IS NOT 'contains responses:': responses present WITHOUT a router is INERT AND CORRECT on both ports (caller_steps wins, D13) and refusing there would break every stock template, since lks init ships templates that document the catalog shape. Guard placed ONCE in execute_scenario_parsed before the provider dispatch, not beside each of the two with_contract_only gates - those are the Gemini and OpenAI branches of one dispatch, and a guard added twice is a guard added once. Error names BOTH remedies, because for a user with no router configured 'use Python' is wrong advice. Deliberately NOT built: no catalog parser, no RouterConfig mirror (SimConfig::router is a RouterPresence - is a router configured and which provider, nothing more), no responses loop in script.rs, and NOT a blanket unconsumed-top-level-key guard, which would make lksr unable to load any scenario in the package since scenario_from_dict does not consume apiVersion/kind while 22 of 23 templates carry both. Scenario::responses holds the RAW value rather than a bool specifically so scenario_to_dict can honour its 'preserve fields on export' contract - a bool would force export to DROP the catalog, the exact mirror of the plan's parse-without-export warning. 11 tests in crates/lks-core/tests/router_guard.rs; cargo fmt clean; cargo test -p lks-core green across 29 binaries. Recorded for the next person: -p lks-core does NOT pull webrtc-sys, so anything under crates/lks-livekit needs -p lks-livekit AND CARGO_TARGET_DIR=C:/t/lksr or the webrtc-sys headers exceed Windows MAX_PATH.

title: Rust hardcodes the validator parity vector list instead of globbing it — a new vector is invisible to lksr
description:
ONE-SIDED SHARED-STATE CONSUMPTION. Real defect, independent of this migration, on exactly the
surface otd.10 governs.

VERIFIED. Python globs the fixture directory; Rust hardcodes a list.
  Python:  tests/test_parity_vectors.py / test_dsl_parity_vectors.py enumerate tests/fixtures/parity/
  Rust:    caller_contract.rs:2153 — `const VALIDATOR_VECTOR_FILES: [&str; 11] = [...]`
           consumed by a hardcoded `for filename in VALIDATOR_VECTOR_FILES` at :2169.
  caller_dsl.rs:764 DOES glob (`fs::read_dir(fixtures_dir())`), which is why the dsl/ subdir is
  safe and this one is not. The asymmetry is the bug.

CONSEQUENCE. Adding a 12th validator_* vector is one-sided BY CONSTRUCTION: Python picks it up
automatically, Rust never sees it, and the "both sides green" claim goes FALSE with nothing going
red. Editing or deleting an existing vector is symmetric and safe. So the harness is quietly
one-way, and its safety degrades precisely as it is used more.

DO: make caller_contract.rs enumerate the same directory the Python side does, then delete
VALIDATOR_VECTOR_FILES. If a curated subset is genuinely wanted, make the exclusion explicit and
fail the test when a validator_*.json file exists that is neither in the list nor in an explicit
skip list — silence is the failure mode, not the subset.

TEST: add a validator vector to tests/fixtures/parity/ and assert the Rust side executes it. If
that test passes before the fix, the harness is not doing what its docstring claims.

WHY P2 AND SEPARATE PR: this migration adds no validator vectors, so nothing here blocks v2. It is
a landmine for the NEXT change. File it; do not fold it into a router diff.
close_reason: commit above. caller_contract.rs now globs tests/fixtures/parity/ for validator_*.json instead of a hardcoded [&str; 11]; VALIDATOR_VECTOR_FILES deleted. caller_dsl.rs already globbed the same directory, so the asymmetry WAS the defect. Verified both directions: adding validator_probe_v30.json with a wrong expected_verdict makes the Rust test FAIL and name the file (so it is really executed), and replacing the glob with a short hardcoded list makes the same test PASS while that vector sits unexecuted - the defect demonstrated, not argued. Both probe vectors removed; cargo fmt --check clean; cargo test -p lks-core green.

title: PRE-EXISTING: two live Rust runtime divergences from the Python contract driver, no bead owns them
description:
PRE-EXISTING DIVERGENCE. Predates the router migration. Demoted to P2/separate PR per the 3tv.7.2
precedent — the migration REVEALS these but did not CREATE them, and folding them in makes the
router diff unreviewable. File them so they have an owner; do not fix them here.

Both are in the LIVE loop, not the dead-code region, which is why "parity means wiring dead code"
does not dispose of them. Verified source-level, both directions:

  1. TRIGGER GAP TOLERANCE MISSING.
     Python: TRIGGER_GAP_TOLERANCE_S = 1.2 (driver.py:58), applied in the agent-speaking loop
     (:1283-1288) and the silence loop (:1305-1310) — only a gap >= 1.2s resets continuous_since,
     so brief VAD dropouts do not disarm a trigger.
     Rust:   lks-livekit/src/script.rs:316-319 — `if !active { trigger_since[arm_idx] = None;
     continue; }`. Hard reset on a SINGLE inactive sample. No gap accumulator anywhere in the loop.
     User-visible: a trigger that Python reliably fires can silently never fire under lksr.

  2. TRIGGER WAIT BUDGET MISSING.
     Python: TRIGGER_WAIT_BUDGET_S = 30.0 (driver.py:45), deadline at :1264; both trigger loops
     return False on expiry, which the call sites turn into FailureReason.BEHAVIOR_TIMEOUT
     (driver.py:388, :489). A never-satisfied trigger FAILS LOUDLY and fast.
     Rust:   script.rs:281-324 has only `elapsed_ms < need -> continue`. ScriptRuntime::run's loop
     (:222) is bounded solely by arm_idx < steps.len() and the stop channel. No wall-clock deadline.
     User-visible: a never-satisfied trigger PARKS THE STEP INDEFINITELY where Python fails in 30s.
     This is the more serious of the two — a hang has no report, a missing fire has a red one.

RELATED, NOTE ONLY (already tracked elsewhere, do not re-file): ENDED_BY and FAILURE_REASONS are
declared at caller_contract.rs:52-72 with ZERO references outside that file; the live failure path is
a free-text Mutex<String> at run.rs:1083-1110. Python returns a typed DriverResult. Same class of
gap — declared-but-dead — but this one is a reporting-fidelity issue, not a hang.

TIEBREAKER IF ANYONE WIRES THE DEAD CODE (v2-32-rtn): two behaviours are Rust-AHEAD and must be
preserved, not deleted. (i) dtmf genuinely EXECUTES on the Rust caller_steps path
(scenario.rs:447-454 -> script.rs:528-543) where Python's driver drops it (driver.py:592-593 —
Python side already tracked). (ii) first_speaker=user handling exists at script.rs:293-306 with no
Python contract-driver equivalent; Python's _wait_trigger (:1239-1312) has no first_speaker concept.

EXIT for this bead: each of the two numbered items either has a Python-pinned golden vector or has
a written "deliberately divergent" note naming which port is right and why. Silence is not an
acceptable close.
notes:
FINDING 2026-09-30 (verified by compile, owner session): the first attempt at this bead was INCOMPLETE and passed every available check.

What was there: `TRIGGER_GAP_TOLERANCE` (:23) and `TRIGGER_WAIT_BUDGET` (:27) declared, `trigger_gap_since` (:228) and `armed_at` (:231) declared, and doc comments that describe BOTH fixes accurately.

What was missing: the fixes themselves.

  1. BUDGET DOES NOT EXIST. `armed_at` is declared at :231 and then discarded at :338 with `let _ = armed_at;`. There is no deadline check, no `sim.script.trigger_timeout` emit, no `Err(RunError)`. A never-satisfied trigger still parks the step until the stop channel - i.e. divergence #2, the one the bead calls the more serious of the two, is STILL PRESENT.

  2. GAP TOLERANCE STILL THE BUG. The comment at :340-344 describes exactly the right fix ("only disarms once the gap reaches TRIGGER_GAP_TOLERANCE_S"), and the code at :347 is still `trigger_since[arm_idx] = None; continue;` - the unconditional reset that IS divergence #1. `trigger_gap_since` is written at :351 and read nowhere.

Why every check passed: it compiles; `cargo test -p lks-livekit` lib is green (11 tests); the doc comments assert the fix is present. Nothing was red. The ONLY signal was the compiler's `dead_code` warnings naming both constants.

This is the most dangerous instance of the pattern this migration has been removing all session ("a knob wearing a working one's clothes", as with `text_planner` and `confidence`) - and worse, because the COMMENT claims the fix exists, so the next reader believes it. Do not accept a comment as evidence that the code beneath it changed.

WHEN WRITING THE TESTS, do not assert timing with real sleeps: Windows `asyncio.sleep` returns up to ~10ms early (see e92901b, where that masqueraded as a flake and was actually the ground truth being wrong). Prefer an injectable tolerance/budget, or assert the CLOCK is consulted rather than that a real-time threshold elapsed.
close_reason: Done, commit d2d0b57. Both divergences fixed to match Python, not documented as divergent, because Python is the reference and divergence #2 is a hang. 1. GAP TOLERANCE: per-step trigger_gap_since records WHEN the condition dropped; the continuity clock resets only once the gap passes TRIGGER_GAP_TOLERANCE = 1200ms (driver.py:58, :1283-1288). The old code reset on a SINGLE inactive sample, so a trigger Python fires reliably could silently never fire under lksr. 2. WAIT BUDGET: TRIGGER_WAIT_BUDGET = 30s (driver.py:45), keyed by arm_idx so advancing starts a fresh budget instead of inheriting a spent one. On expiry it emits sim.script.trigger_timeout and returns Err - never publishes. Before: no deadline at all, so a never-satisfied trigger parked the step until the stop channel. A hang leaves no report; Python fails in 30s and leaves a red one. EXIT CRITERION MET BY FIX + VECTOR for both. tests/trigger_parity.rs, 3 cases, on the REAL driver with real waits - a mocked clock would not catch either bug, since the original defects were a missing accumulator and a missing deadline, both of which a mock satisfies. The budget test asserts the ~30s WINDOW (29-38s band) rather than mere existence of a timeout, per the point that 30 is the contract Python sets, not a detail. MIRROR TEST INCLUDED: a_long_dropout_still_disarms_the_trigger, so the tolerance is not an unbounded latch - a trigger that can never be disarmed is its own hang. MUTATION-VERIFIED, and this is the part worth reading. Reverting gap tolerance to the hard reset fails a_short_dropout and leaves a_long_dropout GREEN - correct, since the old code also disarmed long gaps. Removing the budget fails a_never_satisfied at the 45s guard. PROCESS FAILURE WORTH RECORDING, because a peer caught it and I did not: mid-verification I mutated the source to prove the tests had teeth, then my restore script silently no-opped (its guard pattern did not match), and I carried the MUTANT forward. It compiled, 11 lib tests passed, and the doc comments described the fix while the code beneath them was still the bug. A peer session read the file during that window and diagnosed it from the dead_code warnings. I would not have caught it from a green build. What actually caught it: the peer reading the source, and re-running the tests. Restore scripts that guard on a pattern match and skip silently when it does not match are the hazard - they report success while doing nothing. Verification: lks-livekit lib 11 passed, existing script_runtime 5 passed with no regression, trigger_parity 3 passed, cargo build emits no dead_code warning for either constant. ENVIRONMENT NOTE for whoever builds this next: lks-livekit pulls webrtc-sys, and the default target dir puts its headers at 273 characters, past the Windows MAX_PATH of 260, so the C++ build fails on Cannot open include file for files that demonstrably exist. .cargo/config.toml warned about this at line 1. It needs CARGO_TARGET_DIR=C:/t/lksr (or any short path) in addition to PATH and PYO3_PYTHON. Separately, cargo test -p lks-core does NOT compile webrtc-sys at all, so a green -p lks-core run says nothing about lks-livekit.

title: caller_contract.rs: wire or delete the unreachable parity library
description:
FILE-AND-DECIDE, DO NOT IMPLEMENT HERE. This bead exists so the ~1000-1100 lines of unreachable prod
code in caller_contract.rs have an owner and a date. It must not accrete children — if it starts
growing implementation leaves, it has silently become the Rust epic this migration declined to
open, and that is the failure v2-28-rst's trigger conditions exist to prevent.

MEASURED, tree-wide, not inferred. Symbols with ZERO references outside caller_contract.rs:
plan_speak, plan_dtmf, plan_silence, plan_hangup, plan_backchannel, trigger_barge_in,
verify_semantic_preserving, should_interrupt, interruption_roll, TurnDetector,
RuleBasedSemanticVerifier, classify_agent_silence, validate_with_retry, RunRecord.
That is the entire interaction planner (:1542-1728, mirroring interaction_planner.py:46-133), the
turn detector, the seeded-interruption policy, record/replay (:1728-2118), and the retry helper.
Live surface is ContractValidator, OrchestratorState, evaluate_behavior, is_end_behavior_closing_reply
(script.rs:730-737, :1052, :1070). Roughly HALF the file's prod code is unreachable — not the
75-80% first estimated; the cited clusters sum to ~1000-1100 of ~2121 prod lines.

WHY IT SURVIVED: tests/fixtures/parity/interaction_planner.json, should_interrupt.json,
turn_debounce.json and record_replay.json lock down exactly this dead code, read by
caller_contract.rs's #[cfg(test)] block at :2118. GREEN TESTS OVER UNWIRED CODE — the same class as
commit 665ec8c, and the reason a fixture whose consumer is dead can never go red on its own.

DO: decide per cluster — wire it, or delete it and its fixture. DELETE IS THE DEFAULT BRANCH. The
"wire" branch is only admissible with a named user flow, because AGENTS.md:74 requires
"a concrete user: a real run, a test, or a documented recipe", and the live loop this would attach
to already diverges from Python in the six ways v2-31-div files. Do not leave a third option,
because leaving it IS the current state and the current state is the rot.

IF the migration's removal of the router surface ever proceeds, note that caller_contract.rs's
planner decorates caller_steps — the concept D13 keeps. If D13 is ever superseded, this bead's
scope must be re-derived, not inherited.

EXIT: `cargo test -p lks-core` green with NO vacuous passes. A fixture whose consumer was deleted
must be deleted, not orphaned. Add the non-empty assertion from v2-26-fmt.
notes:
THE BEAD'S PREMISE IS WRONG, and the obvious answer (delete as duplicate) would destroy a capability.

Measured 2026-09-30:

`script.rs` (the LIVE Rust caller path) reuses SEVEN items from caller_contract: BehaviorContract, ContractValidator, OrchestratorState, BehaviorOutcome, EvaluatorVerdict, evaluate_behavior, is_end_behavior_closing_reply. The evaluator and validator are genuinely shared, not re-implemented. Good.

The three "unreachable" symbols are NOT duplicates of it:

  - `plan_speak` (:1630) — the interaction DELIVERY layer (hesitation/stumble tokens from an authored InteractionConfig). script.rs has no equivalent and no need for one: it has no persona-interaction shaping. Not a twin; a different concern.
  - `validate_with_retry` (:1033) — the BOUNDED RETRY wrapper. script.rs constructs `ContractValidator::new(None)` and calls validate directly. So this IS a real gap, but a small one: the live path has no retry loop.
  - `TurnDetector` (:1381) — **not a twin of anything.** It is a 5-state machine (WaitingForAgent / AgentSpeaking / PossibleEnd / AgentTurnComplete / CallerTurn) carrying `chunk_count` and `silence_debounce_ms`. script.rs holds only `trigger_since` / `trigger_gap_since` — "is the agent active, for how long" — and has ZERO references to chunk_count, silence_debounce, or on_agent_audio.

So the two answer DIFFERENT questions:
  - script.rs: WHEN should this step fire?
  - TurnDetector: WHEN did the agent's turn END?

`grep -c "AgentTurnComplete|turn_complete" script.rs` = 0. The live Rust caller has no turn-completion concept at all.

WHY THAT MATTERS RIGHT NOW: "when did the agent's turn end" is precisely PROBLEMS.md §1 — the defect the turn-alignment beads are fixing, and which the peer session is currently measuring against a live duplex agent. So TurnDetector is not dead weight awaiting deletion; it is an UNIMPLEMENTED CAPABILITY for a gap that has a live, open, high-priority problem pointed at it.

REVISED RECOMMENDATION: do NOT delete TurnDetector on this bead, and do not describe it as a duplicate. Deleting it discards the only modelled notion of turn completion in the Rust port, in the same week the project is trying to add one.

If "no dead features" must still be honoured, the honest resolutions are (a) keep it with a written note that it is staged for the turn-alignment work and name the owning bead, or (b) wire it as part of that work. A blind delete is the one option that is wrong on the merits.

For `validate_with_retry`, deleting is defensible ONLY if the live path gains a retry loop in the same change — otherwise the Python/Rust retry semantics diverge, which is the class of bug this whole migration has been removing.

Measured: script.rs (the LIVE Rust path) reuses SEVEN items from caller_contract (BehaviorContract, ContractValidator, OrchestratorState, BehaviorOutcome, EvaluatorVerdict, evaluate_behavior, is_end_behavior_closing_reply) - evaluator and validator are genuinely shared, not re-implemented. title: Pin the five non-SCENARIO contract end_reason keys and the record/replay exclusivity guard
description:
FOUND BY THE PEER SESSION while closing livekit-agent-simulator-dtmf-restore-python-3tv.1, and INDEPENDENT of that revert. Test-only: touches tests/test_contract_live_wiring.py and nothing in src/.

THE GAP
Reverting the c0d3e26 mutants left the test count IDENTICAL (1156 passed, 2 skipped, 2 xfailed, before and after). That is not proof the revert was right. It is proof THE SUITE DOES NOT OBSERVE WHAT THE MUTANTS BROKE.

WHY IT MATTERS
script/models.py:168-174 maps contract_caller_end / contract_agent_end onto the vocab assertions 'sim' / 'agent', and asserts.py:839 special-cases contract_timeout. With the MUTANTC_* labels, EVERY contract run reported its end reason as 'unrecognized' — so every `type: ended_by` assertion naming a side was silently wrong. The mutants were real, not cosmetic; the tests just could not see them.

WHY THE TESTS STAYED GREEN
The four tests that assert end_reason (test_contract_live_wiring.py:379, 443, 711, 773) all reach the ending SCENARIO, which the mutants never touch. The TIMEOUT/TRANSPORT tests (:533, :593) do reach other endings but either raise ContractDriverFailure or discard the return value, so the string is never observed.

SCOPE (test-only)
1. Pin all five non-SCENARIO end_reason keys — caller_end, agent_end, timeout, transport_error, error — through a path that asserts the produced string, not just the failure type.
2. Pin the message format "reason: detail" so a future edit to live_wiring.py:58 is caught.
3. Pin the record_path / replay_path mutual-exclusion guard (live_wiring.py:324-326). This was a FOURTH mutant nobody had listed: without it, run_contract_driver_path(record_path=..., replay_path=...) runs both branches instead of raising. Verify: `git diff c0d3e26~1 -- <the two files>` must stay EMPTY.
4. Keep it in tests/ only. Do NOT touch src/ — the router migration is landing there.

EXIT CRITERION
The new assertions must FAIL against a deliberately reintroduced MUTANTC_ label and pass against the clean tree. A test that passes both ways is exactly the gap this bead closes.

NOTE ON THE BASELINE
1156/2/2 is a FLOOR, not a verdict. Any later bead must show a DELTA above 1156 to prove it added a real assertion; reporting exactly 1156/2/2 means it added none.

The single pass is the SCENARIO parametrisation, which is correct - the mutant never touched that key. The guard test fails with FileNotFoundError on 'run.json', proving the run really fell through to reading the replay file instead of raising, so it detects the deleted guard rather than merely noticing a missing exception. NEW FINDING, relevant to the epic: four of the six map keys are UNREACHABLE in production today. driver.py constructs a failure-free DriverResult at only three sites (SCENARIO x2 at :541/:596, AGENT at :899); every CALLER/TIMEOUT/TRANSPORT/ERROR ending goes through _fail() at :1140, which always attaches a RunFailure, and run_contract_driver_path raises ContractDriverFailure before the map whenever failure is not None. So contract_caller_end, contract_timeout, contract_transport_error, contract_error and the contract_end fallback can never be returned, and the downstream lookups keyed on them (script/models.py:172 contract_caller_end, asserts.py:839 contract_timeout) are themselves dead. I pinned all six anyway, with a docstring stating the unreachability, so a future change that makes one reachable cannot also silently rename it - but this is an AGENTS.md 'no dead features' smell in src/ that someone should triage separately. It also means the real coverage win is the one unmocked test, test_agent_hangup_returns_contract_agent_end, which drives the actual driver to the actual AGENT ending. Tree measures 1185 passed / 2 skipped / 2 xfailed, but only 10 of the +29 are mine; the other 19 are the peer's untracked tests/test_responses.py. Each bead must re-measure at its own start. title: Triage: four unreachable end_reason keys and their dead downstream lookups
description:
FOUND by the peer session while pinning the end_reason labels (bead livekit-agent-simulator-contract-end-reason-coverage-gap-2zo). The pins are done; this is the cleanup they correctly did NOT do, because that bead was test-only.

THE FINDING
4 of the 6 keys in the ended_by map are UNREACHABLE, and the map's dead branches have dead downstream lookups.

WHERE EVERY ending ACTUALLY COMES FROM
  driver.py constructs DriverResult WITHOUT a failure in only three places:
      SCENARIO  :541, :596
      AGENT     :899
  Every CALLER / TIMEOUT / TRANSPORT / ERROR ending goes through _fail() at :1140, and _fail
  ALWAYS attaches a RunFailure. run_contract_driver_path then RAISES ContractDriverFailure before
  the map is ever reached, whenever failure is not None.

SO UNREACHABLE: contract_caller_end, contract_timeout, contract_transport_error, contract_error,
and the contract_end fallback. Only contract_agent_end and contract_scenario_end are live.

DEAD DOWNSTREAM, as a consequence
  script/models.py:172  the contract_caller_end lookup
  asserts.py:839        the contract_timeout special case
Both are branches that no live input can select. This is exactly what made the mutants
undetectable: every contract run reports 'unrecognized', and no assert naming a side could fire.

THIS IS AN AGENTS.md 'no dead features' VIOLATION IN src/, and it predates the router migration.

THE DECISION (owner)
  Option A - DELETE the four dead keys plus the two dead downstream lookups. Cheapest, and matches
              the repo's own rule: contract_timeout / contract_caller_end are speculative queues
              for code that does not exist.
  Option B - CHANGE _fail so a clean ending can carry no failure, which makes the keys reachable
              and gives the map a purpose. More work, and only if something needs those endings.

  Do not do neither. The current state is the one AGENTS.md forbids: surface in src/ that nothing
  can reach.

VERIFICATION
The 2zo pins stay, with their docstring noting unreachable. If Option A lands, delete those pins
for the removed keys IN THE SAME CHANGE so the test file does not start asserting names that no
longer exist. Re-measure the suite at the start: the tree is at 1185 passed / 2 skipped /
2 xfailed, and a stale baseline proves nothing.

title: Verify plugins never run on the caller_steps (contract) path — silent false-pass
description:
FULL REPORT: docs/verify-plugin-contract-path-path.md -> docs/verify-plugin-contract-path.md (read it first; it has the evidence, the proposed shape and the acceptance criteria).

WHY THIS IS P0 DESPITE 'medium' IN THE REPORT
A verify plugin with a deliberately impossible assertion still reports ok: true. That is a silent
false-pass in a test harness, and it invalidates the acceptance gate for the whole response-router
migration: the E2E plugin (.agent-sim/plugins/gpt_live_queue_verify.py) is exactly the kind of
structured event-based assertion this is about, and it would load, register, and never execute. Any
router verdict assertion written through a plugin would be a no-op that looks like a pass.

ROOT CAUSE (verified in the report)
run_orchestrator.py:571-577 hardcodes script_verify = {skipped: True, ...} for the contract path.
evaluate_script_log (script/verify.py:10) is the only caller of registered verify plugins, and it is
reached only from the script_steps branch the skip bypasses. The step-matching half of that function
genuinely does not apply to contract.* events, but the PLUGIN half has no such coupling - a plugin
consumes the run's events, not step ids.

FIX SHAPE (the report's; confirm against src before coding)
Extract the self-contained plugin loop at script/verify.py:194-240 into a helper that takes
(verify, scenario, project_root, events) and returns the plugin-originated checks. Call it from the
CONTRACT branch too, keeping steps_not_applicable and the step-matching skip. Feed plugin failures
into hard_reasons so a failed plugin fails the run the way a failed assert.outcomes already does.

TWO TRAPS THAT COST REAL TIME - BOTH SILENT, both in the report section 6
  - the block key is script_verify:, not verify:  (scenario.py:175)
  - the plugin list is top-level plugin_modules:, not inside script_verify  (scenario_from_dict.py:119)
  - the loader does NOT scan the plugins dir; it opens exactly <name>.py, so the module name must
    equal the filename. ops.py:305-312 warns only when script_verify or plugin_modules is present,
    so misspelling the block key entirely produces no warning at all.
  - plugin_options must be a FLAT map keyed by plugin name (script/verify.py:229), not a nested block.
Any test or scenario written against this bug must use the correct names or it will appear to
pass for the wrong reason - which is the exact failure this bug is about.

ACCEPTANCE (from the report)
1. A plugin with an unsatisfiable assertion FAILS the run, with its reason in hard_reasons.
2. A plugin with satisfiable assertions still passes and changes no existing run.
3. Scenarios without plugin_modules behave exactly as before.
4. lks validate warns on an unregistered plugin name.
5. Plugin check output is persisted in the run artifacts - today it appears NOWHERE, which is why
   this bug was hard to see.

Until fixed, structured event-based assertions are NOT expressible in a scenario; assert natively
with assert.outcomes, or read reports/<run>/events.jsonl from an external summariser.
close_reason:
Fixed and committed. Full report kept at docs/verify-plugin-contract-path.md.

The plugin half of evaluate_script_log was lifted into run_verify_plugins(verify, scenario, project_root, events) and is now called from the contract branch; only the step-matching half stays skipped, which is the part that genuinely does not apply (step_ids vs sim.script.cue). Plugin checks persist under script_verify.plugin_checks, and a failing plugin now sets status=failed - so a plugin assertion is a real gate rather than a no-op that reports ok:true.

7 tests. Source-level test pins the wiring so restoring the blanket skip fails even while the helper still works.

Baseline note: the full suite currently shows 30 failures, but they are NOT from this change - reverting only these two files and this test reproduces the same 30. They come from the peer session's uncommitted live_wiring.py work in the shared tree.

title: Router cannot admit it guessed: off_script is a label, confidence is structurally impossible
description:
FIXES A ROUTER THAT CANNOT ADMIT IT GUESSED. Evidence from live runs 009/011.

THE SYMPTOM (voice-ai-agent-b3, run 011, catalog entry preamble_ack present):

  turn | agent_text                                   | response_id      | correct?
  -----+----------------------------------------------+------------------+---------
    1  | "Thank you for considering our service..."    | callback_number  | NO
    2  | "Are you still there?" (silence kick)          | wrap_up          | NO
    3  | "Goodbye."                                    | off_script       | yes

b3 added a preamble_ack entry to the catalog. It was IN the catalog and the
router STILL ignored it, picking callback_number instead. Consequence: the
agent never receives an answer, goes silent, the silence kick fires, the call
ends. Run 009 (before the entry existed) at least asked for the company name;
011 asks nothing.

WHY THAT PROVES IT IS NOT AN AUTHORING BUG
If the catalog were the control, adding the entry would have fixed it. It did
not, so the decision is not driven by match. Adding vocabulary moves nothing.

TWO ROOT CAUSES, both verified in src/ - NOT inferred

1. `off_script` is a LABEL ON THE CHOICE, not a fallback when nothing fits.
   driver.py:730  `off_script = bool(spec.system)`.
   The system entry is ALWAYS an option - responses.py:239-246
   offerable_ids() docstring: "The system response is always offerable" - and
   the router prompt already says "Choose the system entry ONLY when nothing
   else fits." The model did not use it. NOT because the option was missing,
   but because nothing FORCED it to. An unenforced promise in a prompt.

2. `confidence` is STRUCTURALLY impossible, so the harness has no signal.
   router.py:120-130 build_route_schema declares
       properties: {responseId: ...},  required: [responseId],
       additionalProperties: False
   `additionalProperties: False` forbids the provider from returning
   `confidence` at all. router.py:204 reads raw.get("confidence") and it is
   therefore ALWAYS None - not because the model declined, but because it
   cannot. Confirmed empirically: confidence is null on EVERY decision in every
   run, including the ones that pick correctly.

THE SENTINEL THAT WAS PROPOSED AND REJECTED
Add NO_MATCH="__none__" to the enum. b3 raised it, then withdrew it on the
evidence, and the withdrawal is correct: the system entry is already an enum
value, so a sentinel only lengthens the enum. It adds no signal, which is the
half that is actually missing. Do not reopen it as a cheaper substitute for
this fix.

PROPOSED FIX (b3 agreed; both in router.py, which a5 holds - not started)

  a) Put `confidence` in the schema as a number and add it to `required`.
     Structured Outputs enforce it, so the model always answers with one.
  b) A pick below a threshold is treated as no-match: route to the system
     entry, record off_script: true.
  c) DegeneracyGuard unchanged.

This gives the model a way to REPORT that it is guessing, and the harness a
threshold to CATCH the report. The sentinel only did the second.

THRESHOLD IS NOT FREE - do not guess it
The same b3 finding applies here: `midSessionToolSwap` defaults to true and
its branch had no test. A confidence threshold is exactly the same shape -
a branch that is off until someone notices. It needs a run that MEASURES the
distribution of returned confidences before anyone picks a number, and a test
that fails when the branch is unreachable. A threshold with no measurement
behind it is the same silent no-op in a new coat.

`confidence` IS A DEAD KNOB, AND DELETING IT BREAKS A LEGITIMATE TEST
It has a docstring (router.py:75-77) promising telemetry "so a
low-confidence case can be found", a real consumer (_summarize_router writes
it into decisions[], run_orchestrator.py:156-157) and a test that asserts the
field EXISTS. So it looks alive while being permanently None - the most
dangerous kind, because the test PROTECTS it and deleting the field would
red-light a correct test. Either (a) make it real per the fix above, or
(b) remove field + docstring + the existence assertion together. Leaving both
half-built is the worst outcome. If (b) is chosen, the test that asserts the
field exists must change in the same commit, with a reason.

TEST CONDITIONS - all four, and the fourth is the load-bearing one

  1. The current code cannot distinguish a false `matched` from a genuine one.
     Assert that explicitly, so the fix has something to disprove.
  2. `confidence` is None regardless of what the body returns - prove it by
     feeding a body WITH a confidence and showing it is still discarded.
     That is a structural test, not a model-behaviour test.
  3. confidence is a dead knob (see above; binds whichever option is chosen).
  4. AN ENTRY THAT GENUINELY MATCHES AND IS STILL IGNORED - run 011 turn 1.
     Without this one, "just add the missing entry" stays plausible, which is
     precisely the wrong conclusion run 011 disproved. A bead that keeps only
     1-3 has not recorded why the obvious fix does not work.

VERIFICATION AFTER THE FIX
b3 will drop the now-meaningless preamble_ack entry and re-run, to confirm a
preamble actually lands in off_script. That is the acceptance check, and it
needs a real call - it cannot be established by a unit test alone.

NOT A STUB, NOT A HALF-MEASURE
If confidence cannot be made required in the schema, say so and stop. A
threshold fed by an always-None value is worse than no threshold: it looks
like a guard and catches nothing.
